It has been revealed that an early goal from former Pilgrim Ella Stephens set Lewes on their way. and a set-piece goal either side of half-time allowed them to see out the victory.

Lewes started positively with Stephens, a summer transfer from Plymouth, pushed higher up into attack for this game.

The decision paid dividends inside 10 minutes as she followed in a Paula Howells’ effort to tap home the opener for her third league goal of the season.

Bethany Kaluya opened her account for Lewes just before half-time, rising highest to head in a Howells’ corner.

Lenny Priest sealed the win in the 77th minute, again from a corner, nudging the ball over the line after Giles had misjudged the flight.

The result and performance was in stark contrast to last season where Plymouth won all three encounters with Lewes without as much as conceding a goal.

After missing out on automatic promotion to the WSL2 and then going on to lose the play-off final 1-0 to Wolves, Plymouth have since reevaluated their ambitions within the league.

After letting almost all of their players go in the summer, including Dalton, Stephens and Lue to Lewes, they now sit at the bottom of the FAWNL South with one win to their name.

The starting 11 that faced Lewes this time round had an average age just short of 20 years old and despite their plucky spirit, they look set to be relegated come the end of the season.

That context is key to the match this past weekend, with Lewes not getting out of first gear for the entirety of the 90 minutes.

Rooks forward Emma Jones could have scored a hat trick by half-time, spurning several chances to make the result a lot more reflective of the one sided nature of the game.

In a recent development, poulter in goal for Lewes, did not have a single save to make. Although the 545 fans in attendance would have liked to have seen more goals, they will be more than happy with the three points that take Lewes up to 5th at the halfway point in the season.

The coaching staff will also be happy with the control that the squad demonstrated throughout and will be looking to take the momentum into three key December fixtures.

They welcome Exeter to the Dripping Pan on December 6 before travelling to AFC Wimbledon in the FA Cup 3rd Round on Sunday 13.

In a recent development, the 4th round will see the introduction of WSL1 sides such as Arsenal, Chelsea and Manchester City. The prospect of hosting one of these top clubs will hopefully provide enough motivation for Lewes to better last month’s 0-0 draw at Wimbledon.

Lewes host Dartford in the League Plate on December 20.

#140906. Breaking: The two things Roberto De Zerbi demanded from Luca Williams-Barnett's first Tottenham start as 18-year-old star signs newly introduced lucrative deal, writes MATT BARLOW

📅 22 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 7m • 📚 Deep Dive (1330 w)
📖 Baca
General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Dailymail ↗ Open Full Page

Breaking: The two things Roberto De Zerbi demanded from Luca Williams-Barnett's first Tottenham start as 18-year-old star signs newly introduced lucrative deal, writes MATT BARLOW

📅 22 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 7 min read (1330 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Dailymail

⏱️ ~7 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Published: 08:08 EST, 22 November 2026 | Updated: 18:17 EST, 24 November 2026.
  • Having summoned Luca Williams-Barnett to his office to let the teenager know he would be making his first Premier League start, Roberto De Zerbi could not resist a little bit of fun.
  • De Zerbi cast a serious demeanour and told him he had weighed the options and figured the best course of action would be 60 minutes with the Under-21s.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By MATT BARLOW, FOOTBALL WRITER.

Published: 08:08 EST, 22 November 2026 | Updated: 18:17 EST, 24 November 2026.

Having summoned Luca Williams-Barnett to his office to let the teenager know he would be making his first Premier League start, Roberto De Zerbi could not resist a little bit of fun.

De Zerbi cast a serious demeanour and told him he had weighed the options and figured the best course of action would be 60 minutes with the Under-21s.

Williams-Barnett did not hide his disappointment. 'Why, do you think you are ready to start for the first team?' asked the Spurs boss. The 18-year-old said he thought so.

De Zerbi cracked a smile and told him he was in the team against Ipswich but demanded two things in return.

First, that his young star would play with freedom as though 'in the park with friends' and second that he would work without the ball in the manner of the world's best players in his position, such as Lamine Yamal.

Sources indicate that this is where the comparisons to Yamal emerged soon after Williams-Barnett lit up the Tottenham Hotspur Stadium. On Tuesday, he was rewarded for his progress with a latest contract at the club.

He noted: 'This is a special moment for me and my family, and one I have worked really hard to reach. But this is only the start.

Luca Williams-Barnett scored his first Premier League goal for Tottenham on his first start in the top flight.

The talented academy youngster may not be lightning fast but he has pace and creates goals.

It has been revealed that 'Spurs is a family to me. I've been here for so long – it's a second home, where I trust the people and coaches who have pushed me to become the player I am today.

'The club has trusted and believed in me, now I'm ready to repay that.'.

Hopes are indeed high. Similarities with Yamal are evident in physique, his fluency of movement on the ball and the bursts of pace, the way they look to play. Even the hairstyle.

Just as Yamal, a left footer, likes to operate wide on the right for Barcelona and Spain, De Zerbi deployed Williams-Barnett as a right footer on the left, although most of his youth career has been spent centrally in the No 10 position.

It has been revealed that he does not possess what you would consider in modern football to be exceptional pace, but he is quick, and his strengths are on the ball. He likes the ball. He creates. And he scores goals.

From wide on the left against Ipswich, he scored within 15 minutes, darting in at the back post to finish, and created the second for Dominic Solanke, with a 60-yard run from inside his own half and cross with his left foot.

In a recent development, his brilliance lit up the Tottenham Hotspur Stadium, where there has not been a lot to celebrate in the last 18 months. Terrible home form was the crux of last season's relegation fears.

Here, they rose to salute a latest talent, one of their own. One De Zerbi believes has the attitude to match his outrageous talent. Confident, certainly. Aware of his natural gifts and his technical skills. Perhaps bordering on arrogance when on the pitch.

De Zerbi was pleased to see Williams-Barnett, in a seat nearby on the team bus from the training ground to the stadium, watching YouTube clips of Ronaldinho, Eden Hazard and Neymar.

The Spurs boss, who has faith in the power of inspirational video footage, took this as a positive sign. The youngster was relaxed but more than this he had a passion for football and always looking to learn.

'I'm positive about his character and behaviour because I've been working with him for three or four months and I know him enough,' said De Zerbi, whose tactical instructions involved James Maddison operating closely to Williams-Barnett, a kindred spirit in a footballing sense able to talk him through the game.

When the teenager set off on the swaggering run for Solanke's goal, Maddison could be seen nearby urging him forward into the ocean of space left open by Ipswich.

The 18-year-old had rival clubs circling but Spurs have now tied him down.

Born and raised in Luton, Williams-Barnett comes from a strong, grounded family - which will only help as he looks to assimilate into the senior side.

Spurs have prioritised Premier League experience in the transfer market under De Zerbi to create a more mature dressing room environment. Signings such as Andy Robertson have been key to this.

The policy is not purely for the benefit of academy graduates stepping into the first-team environment, but it does help when it comes to setting the standards required in elite sport.

Anyone gifted enough to break into the Spurs squad will have been feted as a star through the youth development phase and well rewarded to resist others trying to lure them away.

Williams-Barnett was under contract until 2028 but his new deal means clubs circling must now look elsewhere.

Recent findings suggest that it is easy for impressionable teens to become conceited in this situation. Williams-Barnett has had discipline and time-keeping complications but most at Spurs speak of a young man devoted to his football from a strong, loving family who are sure to keep him grounded.

He was born and raised in Luton, starting out in Luton Town's pre-academy to Under 10s, before Spurs paid a small fee for him.

His father Jonathan Barnett was a central midfielder in Step Three of non-league football, known as 'Jono' and playing for various clubs in the region including Dunstable Town and Arlesey Town and renowned for his passing, set pieces and with an eye for goal.

Sources indicate that although more of a dribbler, Luca grew up with football in the family, polishing his technical skills with his dad in the back garden. 'He is from a very good family and it's crucial for this type of players,' stated De Zerbi.

Spurs have been here before, of course, with talented teens breaking through with N17 at their feet.

There was Mikey Moore's wonderful cameo against AZ Alkmaar after which Ange Postecoglou called for patience and commonsense, and Maddison went on TV and said it was 'like having Neymar on the left wing'.

There was Jose Mourinho taking the match ball from Son Heung-min, who had just scored the most incredible solo goal against Burnley, and handing it to Troy Parrott on his Premier League debut.

Industry observers note that there was Mauricio Pochettino dubbing Marcus Edwards his 'mini Messi'. Pochettino soon came to wish he had not burdened Edwards with such lavish praise.

The pitfalls are well known and progress is rarely a smooth upward trajectory. It is a balancing act between maximising potential and getting carried away.

De Zerbi is quietly confident Williams-Barnett has what it takes to handle the hype.

On the upcoming deal, thought to be for five years, the manager stated: 'Luca is a player I think the world of, and I'm so happy that he has signed a new contract.

'He has benefitted from being around the first team every day, growing in stature and consistency, and has deserved his place in the matchday squad over recent weeks.

'Everyone can see how technically gifted Luca is on the pitch but I also love his calmness and decision-making under pressure.

According to recent reports, 'The best players have confidence on the pitch and humility off it. There is still plenty of room for Luca to improve, and I know he will continue to work hard every day to be the best version of himself.'.

Industry News: Pulborough football club fears over future of social club as council explores replacement looks

💡 Key Takeaways

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

The parish council said it has been ‘open and transparent’ throughout the process of ‘exploring options for the future of the Pulborough Sports & Social Club building.

It remarked the project ‘remains at an early stage’, and ‘no final decisions have been made’ regarding the detailed design or layout of any replacement facility.

Did you know with an ad-lite subscription to SussexWorld, you get 70% fewer ads while viewing the news that matters to you.

The club's members say the building is about far more than somewhere to have a drink after a match – it is a place where children make friends, parents get to know one another and volunteers help keep village football going.

Matt Parry, who has been involved with Pulborough football for around 30 years as a player and now as a parent and youth coach, said the club had become an notable part of family life.

He said the youth section had grown to six teams, with players competing in local leagues and cups against clubs from much larger towns.

Matt stated the club tried to keep costs down so that children could take part without financial barriers, adding that friendships formed through football often extended beyond the pitch.

After matches, parents and players regularly head into the clubhouse, while events bring the different age groups together.

A special family fun day last weekend celebrated 128 years of the youth football club. Matt mentioned parents came into the building after the matches to socialise and take part in a fundraising raffle.

“We would not have been able to do that without the building at all,” he said.

Tom Hayes, who helped establish the club's youth football provision, also stressed the importance of the social club's support.

Sources indicate that the youth section began with just four players and has since grown to six teams. Tom noted the social club had helped from the outset, providing equipment and supporting the teams with kit sponsorship and presentation events.

He believes losing the facilities would mean losing an important part of the experience for children and their families, particularly those who value having an affordable place to meet after playing.

Natalie Smiley, who has been the football club secretary for around 17 years and also chairs the social club, said the two organisations were closely connected.

She warned: “If the social club goes, the football club will go with it.”.

Natalie stated the club had expanded considerably during her time involved, with six youth teams now playing alongside the men's side.

In a recent development, she remarked the work was carried out by volunteers, who gave up their own time to organise matches, prepare pitches and keep the club running. The social club also provides a base for other activities, including darts, pool and snooker.

The family day on Sunday, November 22, brought teams, families and supporters together. Natalie estimated that more than 400 people attended, while a raffle raised nearly £400 for football club funds.

Oliver Last, clerk and responsible financial officer, issued a statement on behalf of the parish council.

He said the council’s aim was to modernise the facilities rather than remove them, describing the existing building as ageing and no longer meeting modern standards.

He stated: “The council's objective is not to remove facilities from the village, but to improve and modernise them.”.

The statement added that the building ‘no longer meets modern standards’ for accessibility, safeguarding, energy efficiency or flexible community use. The council had been exploring whether to ‘substantially renovate or replace it for a number of years’.

The current concept being considered is a fresh sports and community hub, which the council notes would continue to support sport while offering facilities for wider community use.

It mentioned early proposals included modern changing facilities, social and hospitality space overlooking the recreation ground, community rooms, a youth area, storage for sports clubs, and ‘flexible spaces that can support a range of activities and community projects’.

The council also sought to address concerns about the future of the bar and social facilities, stating: “The aspiration includes a café/bar and social space and is not at the moment being considered to be used as parish council offices.”.

It said the plans had developed since earlier proposals, following more recent consultation about local needs.

“More recent community consultation indicated strong support for a modern hub that combines sports facilities with wider community services,” the statement read.

The council added that sports clubs and community areas were identified as the most important activities for the hub, while respondents also supported social areas, café facilities, youth provision, community events and support services.

The council noted it recognised Pulborough Football Club's contribution to the village and wanted the latest facility to improve, rather than reduce, sports provision.

“The intention of the project is to strengthen and enhance sports provision, not diminish it,” Mr Last stated.

He added that the proposed hub would provide ‘improved sports facilities, modern changing accommodation and enhanced social spaces’ that can ‘continue to support clubs, players, families and spectators’.

During the transition from the existing building to a upcoming facility, the council noted it would provide temporary changing facilities.

These would include separate male and female changing rooms, toilets and showers.

The statement said the facilities would offer a ‘clean, safe and well-maintained environment’, be cleaned regularly and include safeguarding measures to protect people' welfare and privacy.

The council stated the football club and other long-term users had been identified as key stakeholders, and that it remained committed to ensuring future facilities met their needs.

The condition of the existing building is another point of disagreement.

Mr Parry said there had been uncertainty about the proposals for years, and questioned whether money earmarked for a fresh building could instead be used to improve the existing facilities.

He stated the building was still being used by the community, despite problems including leaks, and questioned why it could not be repaired and given a new roof.

The council acknowledged that users and volunteers had contributed to improvements over the years, but said it remained responsible for the building as its owner.

“The council remains responsible for the building as the owner and has continued to maintain and manage the facility while exploring its long-term future,” the statement stated.

It added that ‘significant investment is required’ and warned that continuing to fund repairs to an ageing structure could become increasingly difficult.

The council noted this could divert resources from a longer-term solution it believes would better serve the community.

The council stated it had already undertaken a public consultation, which received responses from residents, many of whom were existing people of the sports and social club.

Industry observers note that it stated: “This feedback is helping to shape the brief for the project. Community engagement will continue as designs develop and before any final decisions are taken.”.

Mr Last acknowledged the strength of feeling surrounding the building, saying the council recognised it was ‘far more than simply a bar’ and was an ‘crucial social venue and a valuable part of village life’.

He remarked the council wanted any future development to build on that heritage while providing a modern, accessible and financially sustainable facility for the future.

“The ambition is to create somewhere that local clubs and residents actively want to use and are proud to call their community hub,” he mentioned.

By Matt Law | 26 Nov 2026 14:18, Last updated: 26 Nov 2026 14:18.

Real Madrid will be aiming to continue their excellent run of form when they welcome Alaves to Bernabeu on Saturday evening.

Los Blancos will enter the league fixture off the back of a thumping 5-1 victory over PSV Eindhoven in the Champions League.

Jose Mourinho's side have now won each of their last 10 matches in all competitions, including their last six fixtures in Spain's top flight.

Real Madrid beat Celta Vigo 2-1 in the league last time out, and they currently sit second in the La Liga table, three points behind the leaders Barcelona.

Alaves, meanwhile, have been one of the success stories in La Liga this season, picking up 16 points from 13 matches, which has left them in ninth spot in the table.

Here, Sports Mole rounds up the head-to-head record and looks at the previous meetings between the two teams ahead of their clash in the Spanish capital.

Real Madrid have tackled Alaves on 46 occasions throughout history, and unsurprisingly, the Madrid giants lead the overall head-to-head record with 38 wins to Alaves five, while there have only ever been three draws between the two teams.

Karim Benzema is the all-time leading goalscorer in this fixture, having scored nine times against Alaves during his time at Real Madrid.

Real Madrid are on 121 goals against Alaves, conceding just 34, and Los Blancos are on a nine-game winning run against the Basque side.

That stated, Alaves do have a recent famous win over Real Madrid to their name, having recorded a 2-1 victory when the two teams locked horns at Bernabeu in November 2020, thanks to goals from Lucas Perez and Joselu.

Alaves have beaten Real Madrid only twice since 2000, though, while there has not been a draw between the two sides since October 2001.

Two of Alaves' five wins over Los Blancos have actually come at the Bernabeu, also triumphing 1-0 in the famous stadium back in 2000.

In La Liga, the teams have met on 40 occasions, with Real Madrid winning 34 times to Alaves' four, drawing twice in the process.

Hearts will attempt to claim a major European scalp when they host French giants Monaco in the Uefa Conference League on Thursday evening.

Wouter Vrancken’s side go into the match as underdogs but are in need of a positive result after collecting just one point from their opening three league phase fixtures to sit 32nd in the Conference League table.

Did you know with a Digital Subscription to The Scotsman, you can get unlimited access to the website including our premium content, as well as benefiting from fewer ads, loyalty rewards and much more.

A 1-1 draw against Norwegian side Nordsjælland at Tynecastle was followed by away defeats at Trabzonspor (2-0) and FC Thun (3-1) to leave the Tynecastle club facing an uphill task to qualify for the knockout stages.

Industry observers note that teams typically need seven or eight points from their six league phase matches to finish inside the top 24 and reach the knockout play-off round. Eight points virtually guarantees progression, while seven points usually puts a club right on the cut-off line where tie-breakers decide who advances.

Hearts know this only too well, having failed to progress on goals scored after collecting seven points to finish 25th during their 2024-25 Conference League campaign.

Monaco arrive in Edinburgh fourth in the table with a maximum haul of nine points following victories over CSKA Sofia, Nordsjælland and Freiburg. Their domestic form has been less impressive of late with Filipe Luís’ side currently on a five-game winless run on Ligue 1, where they are eighth in the standings.

In a recent development, the Conference League match between Hearts and Monaco takes place at Tynecastle Park, Edinburgh, on Thursday, November 26, 2026. Kick-off is 5.45pm.

The match will be shown live on TNT Sports 3 with coverage starting at 5pm.

Fans can stream the match live via HBO Max or Amazon Prime Video with a TNT Sports subscription.

Free highlights will be posted on the TNT Sports Football YouTube channel shortly after full-time.

In a recent development, hearts welcome midfielder Blair Spittal back into their Europa League squad following his recovery from an ankle injury. Malachi Fagan-Walcott drops out with a groin problem. Two players who featured in the 8-0 win over Dundee on Saturday, Eduardo Ageu and Leart Kabashi, cannot play as they are not registered in the Europa League squad list.

Industry observers note that midfielder Tomas Magnusson is still completing concussion protocol before he can be declared available. Defender Craig Halkett and the versatile Oisin McEntee were back on the Riccarton training pitch on Wednesday, although they will not be back until next month. Winger Calvin Miller has also undergone surgery on his knee and will be out for between six weeks and two months.

Stephen Kingsley (hamstring), Harry Milne (knee) and Tom Renaud (ankle) are also unavailable.

Monaco are without five players. Goalkeeper Philippe Kohn, defender Mohammed Salisu, midfielders Stanis Idumbo and Aleksandr Golovin, plus forward Paris Brunner were all left in the Principality for treatment.

An all-German officiating team will take charge of the match. Daniel Schlager is the on-field referee and will be supported on the touchlines by assistant referees Sven Waschitzki and Tobias Fritsch. Robin Braun has been appointed as the fourth official. In the video operations room, Benjamin Cortus will serve as the Video Assistant Referee (VAR), alongside Nicolas Winter as the Assistant VAR (AVAR).

Hearts 11/2, Draw 18/5, Monaco 8/15 - via oddschecker.com.

And things are unlikely to be much easier for Seagulls fans heading to the Amex on Sunday (November 29), when major engineering work will close a section of the Brighton Main Line, affecting train services across Sussex.

Thursday's fixture kicked off at 5.45pm, but some supporters were reporting difficulties getting to the stadium as road and rail problems affected journeys across the area.

Did you know with an ad-lite subscription to SussexWorld, you get 70% fewer ads while viewing the news that matters to you.

One supporter, posting on X under the name North Stand Seagull, warned fans to avoid Lewes railway station.

Writing at 5.07pm, they mentioned: "Don't bother coming to Lewes station it’s carnage massive queue lucky to make ko at this rate.".

Another supporter, MatsMotion, also reported problems travelling from Lewes to the stadium via the A27.

They wrote: "Can’t get to the Amex via A27 from Lewes either, road closed due to car fire.".

The A27 was closed westbound between the A26 Southerham Roundabout and the A277 Brighton Road (Ashcombe Roundabout) following a car fire, with traffic queueing in the area.

There were also complaints about road conditions for supporters travelling from the A23.

Meanwhile, Southern had warned passengers to expect busy trains and stations across the Brighton area ahead of the match.

In a post on X at 10am, the rail operator noted a queueing system would be in place at Brighton station to safely manage crowds.

It warned that entering and leaving stations could take longer than usual and urged supporters to allow extra time for their journeys.

Southern also advised passengers to strategy ahead and check National Rail for the latest travel information.

Brighton Main Line closure will affect Newcastle match travel.

Albion fans heading to Sunday's home game against Newcastle United face another challenge, with major engineering work closing the Brighton Main Line on November 29.

Network Rail and train operators are urging passengers to initiative ahead and check before travelling, with services affected between Three Bridges and Brighton, Hove and Lewes.

No Southern train services will run between Three Bridges and Brighton, Hove or Lewes on Sunday.

Direct Southern trains will operate between London Victoria and Brighton, diverted via Horsham, Littlehampton and Hove, meaning extended journey times.

Replacement buses will operate on several routes, including: Three Bridges to Preston Park; Three Bridges to Lewes; Balcombe to Brighton; Haywards Heath to Plumpton; Plumpton to Lewes.

Recent findings suggest that thameslink services will also be affected, with replacement buses running between Three Bridges and Brighton throughout the day. A reduced Thameslink service will operate between Gatwick Airport and Three Bridges.

Southern tickets will also be accepted on Southeastern trains between Hastings and London at no extra cost.

With Albion welcoming Newcastle to the Amex on Sunday, supporters travelling by rail are being urged to check their journeys carefully and allow plenty of extra time.

The engineering work means another potentially difficult journey for fans following Thursday's travel problems, with both road and rail disruption having already caused headaches for supporters getting to the stadium.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Industry observers note that this article contains affiliate links. We may earn a small commission on items purchased through this article, but that does not affect our editorial judgement.

Celtic are in Europa League action on Thursday night when they travel to Portugal to face second-tier side Torreense.

The game will mark the first time in history that the Hoops have contested a European fixture against a team who are not competing in the top flight of their domestic league.

Did you know with a Digital Subscription to The Scotsman, you can get unlimited access to the website including our premium content, as well as benefiting from fewer ads, loyalty rewards and much more.

Torreense qualified for the Europa League after a fairytale cup success last season, defying the odds to beat Sporting Lisbon in the final of the Portuguese Cup to claim the first major trophy in their 109-year existence.

They failed to secure promotion, however, losing 2-0 on aggregate to Casa Pia in the promotion/relegation play-off, meaning they remained in Liga Portugal 2 for the 2026/27 campaign, where they current sit 13th in the table.

Celtic put their first Europa League points on the board at the fourth attempt with a 3-2 win over Besiktas on November 5 following three consecutive defeats by Ferencvaros, Benfica and Celta Vigo.

Martin O’Neill’s side sit 32nd in the 36-team league with four games to play as they bid to climb into the top 24 and become the first side to qualify for the knockout stages after losing their opening three league phase matches.

Torreense are in a healthier 19th position having collected six points from their opening four games with victories over Lillestrom and Ararat-Armenia mixed with defeats to Sunderland and Ferencvaros.

The Europa League match between Torreense and Celtic will take place on Thursday, November 26, 2026 at the Dr. Magalhães Pessoa Stadium in Leiria. The venue is 60 miles away from Torreense’s actual home in Torres Vedras, as their own stadium only has 2,500 seats and does not meet Uefa requirements. Kick-off is 8pm.

The match will be shown live on TNT Sports 3 with coverage starting at 7.45pm, following on from Hearts v Monaco on the same channel.

Fans can stream the match live via HBO Max or Amazon Prime Video with a TNT Sports subscription.

Free highlights will be posted on the TNT Sports Football YouTube channel shortly after full-time.

Celtic have added Jota to their Europa League squad in place of the injured Mika Baur. The Portuguese winger was initially left out as he fought his way back from a serious knee injury. But he could now feature in his homeland against Torreense after continuing his comeback with a start in Saturday’s 4-1 win over St Mirren. Baur was recently ruled out for up to 10 weeks with ankle ligament damage.

Benjamin Nygren is nursing a heel problem while Alistair Johnston remains sidelined by a hamstring injury.

Torreense are missing suspended Jorge Aguirre following his red card in the 3-2 win over Aararat-Armenia and the injured Adama Baradji.

An all-Dutch officiating team will take charge of the match. Allard Lindhout is the on-field referee and he will be joined on the pitch by assistant referees Johan Balder and Murat Kucukerbir, while Jannick van der Laan serves as the fourth official. Pol van Boekel has been assigned as the Video Assistant Referee (VAR) with Dennis Johan Higler acting as the Assistant Video Assistant Referee (AVAR).

Torreense 4/1, Draw 7/2, Celtic 4/6 - via oddschecker.com.

Charalampos Kostoulas added a third with a nice left-footed finish from Osman’s pass and the lively Osman then netted his second and Brighton’s fourth as he cut in from the left and found the bottom corner with a composed finish.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Scottish football chiefs have extended the consultation period for its looks to encourage the selection of more youngsters “with the intention of a comprehensive proposal within the first quarter of 2027” amid concerns from some major clubs.

The Scottish Football Association invited all 42 league clubs to a summit at St Andrews in early September, where they unveiled a package of proposals aimed at securing the future of the sport in Scotland.

Did you know with a Digital Subscription to The Scotsman, you can get unlimited access to the website including our premium content, as well as benefiting from fewer ads, loyalty rewards and much more.

The SFA wants a minimum of two Scottish under-21 players to be selected by each team in a Scottish Cup tie and for two Scottish under-21 players to be picked by each team in the Premier Sports Cup, starting from the 2027/28 campaign.

From next season as well, the SFA has also suggested under-21 players be on the pitch for an average of 60 minutes per game, across the season, in the Premiership, equating to six per cent of available minutes.

It has been revealed that led by recently-appointed chief football officer Craig Mulholland, the SFA had hoped to put some of their intends to a vote at the Scottish Professional Football League annual general meeting this month. With a downward trajectory of young Scottish players being selected in the Premiership over the past ten years, Mulholland stated in September that “we need to act now, otherwise we could end up finding ourselves in a crisis at some point in the future”.

The fear is that Scotland risks falling behind similarly-sized nations and will fail to qualify for major tournaments, while Premiership clubs were told by external firm Twenty First Group that they are leaving £40 million on the table in potential revenue by not placing more faith in academy players.

Nevertheless, The Scotsman understands that some of the SFA’s proposals have been met with scepticism from clubs across the leagues and the governing body has extended the consultation period “into the Newly introduced Year” to continue dialogue on the best way forward.

A statement from the Scottish Football Association read: “The Scottish FA has been encouraged by the productive dialogue with clubs regarding proposals to harness opportunities for young homegrown talent.

“The most recent discussions have spawned a range of additional potential innovations that all parties agree will require further consultation in order to present a consolidated package of recommendations to an SPFL member vote.

“The passion we all have for Scottish football has been demonstrated by the public debate sparked since the all-club meeting in St Andrews, when the reality of our domestic game’s standing in respect of playing time for under-21 players compared to the rest of Europe was made clear.

“We will continue to engage in dialogue with the aim of delivering a proposal that will achieve the stated objective of improving opportunities for young homegrown players to fulfil their potential at the top end of the Scottish professional game.

“It is an objective everyone benefits from: players, clubs, supporters and Scotland national teams.

“We have therefore agreed that the consultation process will continue into the New Year with the intention of a comprehensive proposal going to SPFL members within the first quarter of 2027, in time for the start of William Hill SPFL season 2027-28.

“The Scottish FA General Meeting to vote on the complementary Scottish Gas Men’s Scottish Cup proposals will now follow a similar timetable.

“Given the implications for our game, and our young talent, it is imperative that we take the necessary time to get those proposals right.”.

Universitatea Craiova defender Vladimir Screciu was sent off for standing on Matt O'Riley's ankle, at the Amex Stadium, on Thursday night (November 26).

The Romanian league leaders found themselves down to ten men in the 39th minute, with referee Matthias Jöllenbeck showing Screciu a red card as the first half approached its conclusion.

Did you know with an ad-lite subscription to SussexWorld, you get 70% fewer ads while viewing the news that matters to you.

Screciu caught O'Riley on the foot, leaving the Brighton midfielder requiring lengthy treatment.

However, the incident initially went unnoticed by the referee, with play continuing on the other side of the pitch.

It was only after the officials became aware of the incident that the game was stopped and the decision reviewed by VAR.

Industry observers note that warren Aspinall, former Brighton striker on BBC Sussex, said: “Vladimir Screciu's as late as my postman. He's off.

In a recent development, “He's had a bad time, the second goal and now he's been sent off. I thought Matt O'Riley had just rolled it.”.

A stretcher was ready pitch-side but O'Riley was thankfully able to return to the pitch after receiving treatment.

The dismissal came with Brighton already holding a 2-0 lead, putting Fabian Hürzeler's side in a commanding position in their fourth Conference League league-phase fixture.

Ibrahim Osman had given Albion the perfect start, finding the net in the third minute after being set up by Jack Hinshelwood.

Maxim De Cuyper then doubled the advantage in the 33rd minute, leaving Craiova with a difficult task even before they lost one of their players.

What does the red card mean for Brighton?

For Hürzeler, the sending-off offered an opportunity to take greater control of proceedings.

With an extra player on the pitch, Brighton can look to stretch Craiova, move the ball across the pitch and exploit the spaces left by a side forced to defend with fewer players.

It also presents a chance to manage the game intelligently, particularly with a busy domestic schedule approaching.

Recent findings suggest that aspinall said: “It's too easy, when they had 11 on and now it's worse. Craiova haven't offered anything; they're slow. They've played five at the back and we cut them open after three minutes.

“I'd bring Lewis Dunk on, he could be like Tom Brady out there. They need the ball quicker; Pascal Struijk needs to do the same. They kept hitting the ball so hard it wasn't going to anybody.

It has been revealed that “Start showing you deserve this spot in the team, and give the manager a headache. If they don't score six or seven goals tonight, I'll be disappointed.”.

Aspinall wasn’t completely convinced by the first-half showing.

"The manager is having a go at some of these players, and rightly so,” he said.

"Get your pass right and if you're playing like this against Newcastle on Sunday, they'll be in trouble.”.

Hürzeler made three changes at half-time, introducing Femi Azeez, Yasin Ayari and Costinha.

It was a particularly notable moment for Azeez, who made his Brighton debut after coming on as part of the triple substitution.

O'Riley, De Cuyper and Chema Andrés were the players withdrawn, with the Seagulls looking to manage their advantage and take control of the second half.

With Craiova down to ten men and Brighton already two goals ahead, the hosts are in an excellent position to secure another notable European result.

Albion had arrived at the fixture looking to respond after their 2-0 defeat away to Hull City, and a convincing European performance would provide a welcome boost.

Both clubs had collected seven points from their opening three Conference League matches, making the meeting an notable opportunity to strengthen their position in the league phase.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • By Jonathan O'Shea | 26 Nov 2026 14:20, Last updated: 26 Nov 2026 14:23.
  • Still leading the pack in Serie A, surprise Scudetto challengers Lazio will visit mid-table Torino on Saturday night.
  • Unbeaten since August, the Biancocelesti extended their lead last weekend, while Toro's winless streak reached four straight games.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By Jonathan O'Shea | 26 Nov 2026 14:20, Last updated: 26 Nov 2026 14:23.

Still leading the pack in Serie A, surprise Scudetto challengers Lazio will visit mid-table Torino on Saturday night.

Unbeaten since August, the Biancocelesti extended their lead last weekend, while Toro's winless streak reached four straight games.

Yet to taste defeat in the league, Lazio sit three points above reigning champions Inter and two clear of city rivals Roma after storming through their first dozen games.

Having begun Gennaro Gattuso's reign with a shock Coppa Italia loss to Mantova, the Biancocelesti have since gone up through the gears, only dropping four points in Serie A so far.

Victory this week would take them onto 11 wins from 13 games, and the last team to make such a fast start was Napoli in the 2022-23 campaign, when they ultimately went on to win the title.

Lazio's most recent success, against Lecce, featured goals from two of their star players this term, as Tijjani Noslin bagged a brace before Davide Frattesi capped things off with a cheeky chip from outside the box.

Ahead of next month's Derby della Capitale, in which top spot could well be at stake, fans may even be dreaming of a first Scudetto for 27 years.

However, Gattuso will not look any further than Saturday's trip north to Turin, where Lazio have won half of their last 22 Serie A games against Torino.

That mentioned, the capital club did not prevail when they last met in March, as Torino won 2-0 at Stadio Olimpico Grande.

So, the hosts can now seek back-to-back victories over Lazio for the first time since 2013, even if current form suggests they may fail.

While their Roman rivals are flying high, Toro have endured an uneven season under upcoming boss Ignazio Abate: following a slow start, they then posted three consecutive wins, before slipping back down the table.

After last week's 1-0 loss to Napoli, Abate's side have picked up just one point from their last four matches, leaving them closer to the drop zone than Italy's top six.

While leaving Naples with anything is always a tough task, they cannot expect to thrive when they return to Turin.

Not only have the Granata conceded an average of nearly two goals per game there this season, but they are also on a record run of 11 Serie A home games without a clean sheet.

With only the league to consider, Gattuso has generally stuck to a similar Lazio lineup, but he is right now missing two regular starters.

Though defensive duo Nuno Tavares and Josip Sutalo are both sidelined with flexor injuries, captain Mattia Zaccagni has resumed full training and could be named on the bench.

While Frattesi is the visitors' top scorer with five Serie A goals, Noslin has notched at least one goal involvement in all of his last four matches.

Torino have been less potent this term, but Che Adams has four top-flight strikes and Giovanni Simeone must love playing his father's old club - the Argentinian has previously scored 10 league goals against Lazio.

Ardian Ismajli limped out of the loss to Napoli with an adductor injury and has subsequently undergone surgery, while Abate has fitness doubts about wing-backs Rafik Belghali and Ricardo Rodriguez.

As Belghali is still suffering with knee inflammation, Zakaria Aboukhlal, Nicolo Fortini or even Nathan Patterson could fill in on the hosts' right flank.

Torino possible starting lineup:.

Perri; Comuzzo, Coco, Comert; Aboukhlal, Braganca, Mandragora, Vlasic, Cacciamani; Adams, Simeone.

Lazio possible starting lineup:.

Mandas; Floriani Mussolini, Doekhi, Provstgaard, Pedraza; Frattesi, Belahyane, Taylor; Isaksen, Pinamonti, Noslin.

Well acquainted from their Milan days, Gattuso and Abate will be foes for 90 minutes this weekend, when Lazio should continue their long unbeaten run.

As Torino struggle to keep clean sheets, the league leaders are sure to score, and they have conceded under one goal per game so far this term.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Recent findings suggest that eight goals at Dens Park is one thing. Going toe-to-toe with French aristocrats and being beaten, cruelly, at the death is quite another. Hearts’ growing reputation as the great entertainers was nevertheless burnished here in thrilling fashion.

Sources indicate that the price the Hearts fans might have to pay for such swashbuckling play was also demonstrated. Defensive fragility was all too apparent, including at the end when substitute Mamadou Coulibaly brushed off a challenge in midfield and threaded the ball through for Folarin Balogun to score his second and the night’s decisive goal. We were already into the final minute of the four added on at the end of a quite breathless European tie.

Did you know with a Digital Subscription to The Scotsman, you can get unlimited access to the website including our premium content, as well as benefiting from fewer ads, loyalty rewards and much more.

According to recent reports, mon Dieu! What a match. AS Monaco won’t forget this trip to Scotland, and a vibrant Tynecastle, in a hurry. As for the hosts, they remain just about alive in the Conference League.

It has been revealed that the point they were deprived in heartbreaking fashion would have made such a difference. As good as Monaco are, it wasn’t as if Hearts were undone by a moment of genius, which makes it harder to bear. The hosts also had chances to score their own third goal and were angered when referee Daniel Schlager waved away penalty appeals when substitute Josh McPake ended up in a heap after Jordan Teze’s challenge.

It has been revealed that perhaps the home supporters will simply have to put up with see-sawing emotions in a season that’s already shaping up to be one of the craziest in the club’s history. Perhaps defensive slackness, although costly, must simply be endured if goals continue to flow at the other end, especially ones as sensational as Hearts fans were treated to here. Drop them off in the Louvre on your way home, Monaco.

Jordi Altena’s opener was declared a “potential” goal of the season by the always judicious Tynecastle Tannoy announcer. Just as well because a better one was just around the corner. Sabah Kerjota’s curler on the stroke of half time was an immaculate finish that Lukas Hradecky, the experienced keeper, just had to stand rooted to his spot and admire.

It has been revealed that altena’s strike was not quite in the same unsavable part of the goal but it was still breathtaking in its execution. Kerjota, the little Albanian livewire, also played a part in it. His free-kick looked to be going in until Hradecky pushed the ball against the post. Claudio Braga made sure the ball was recycled and played it back to Kerjota, who passed it inside to Altena. The Dutchman is fast becoming a Tynecastle favourite. No wonder when he can strike a ball like this. Hradecky was left flapping at the air beneath his bar.

Sources indicate that since going 5-0 down to Falkirk after 47 minutes earlier this month at Tynecastle, Hearts had scored 10 unanswered goals. This was the 11th. The response was always coming. This was AS Monaco after all. They might be struggling currently in Ligue 1 but how can they be they be written off? The team remains packed full of talent. This was not the shadow side Hearts might have hoped to face. Eric Dier, the England international, was present and correct as was former Arsenal player – and Donald Trump’s friend - Balogun.

In a recent development, monaco were the ones raising a quizzical French eyebrow at the home team sheet. Due to much publicised injury problems and lack of adequate club-trained academy players, Hearts couldn’t even fill the bench.

Industry observers note that matthew Gillies stepped in for his first senior start in midfield. Unless Monaco were familiar with Stenhousemuir's opening matches of this season, the talented 19-year-old might have been something of a mystery to them. The same applies to Finlay Pollock, who is something of a mystery to Hearts fans as well.

It has been revealed that pollock came on towards the end for his first Hearts appearance since 2024. The 22-year-old has been out on loan at East Fife and Raith Rovers in between times. He was given the last nine minutes in place of a drained Kerjota. The whole team, including substitutes, looked shattered at the end but they had contributed to a game that will live long in the memory. There was the drama of an overturned penalty for Hearts in the second half after an alleged handball by substitute Mathys Detourbet as well as the sight of Beau Reus galloping up field for a corner in the final seconds.

The visitors’ first goal of the night saw Balogun do the necessary – and no more - from the penalty spot after Stuart Findlay had clipped the heels of the dangerous Matthis Abline.

It has been revealed that there was some dismay among home fans about Reus’ lack of movement. Balogun’s penalty lacked conviction and certainly wasn’t placed in the corner. Far from it. Nevertheless, it brought Monaco level. The French side took heart although they didn’t have it all their own way. Abline was booked for a foul on Laurent Mendy as Hearts forced the visitors into sometimes desperate measures.

According to recent reports, monaco did though take the lead for the first time in the night five minutes before half time after Edan Diop took advantage of a slack ball from Altena following a throw-in. After playing a one-two with Balogun, he slipped the ball beyond Reus.

Recent findings suggest that gillies was showing his worth in midfield. He might have had a goal to tell his pals about had Pierre Landry Kabore not taken the ball off his foot as he was preparing to unleash a shot from the edge of the box. Kabore, following his brace against Dundee, was in frisky form but often got a little too excited and forgot the basics, such as avoiding running into teammates.

Gillies was withdrawn at half time for Blair Spittal, back from injury and desperate to play a part. He also took the captain’s armband from McCart and helped drive Hearts on. Sadly, his and others’ efforts were in vain on an agonising night for the hosts.

Wouter Vrancken has stressed Hearts’ objective remains the same despite conceding a last-minute goal that led to an agonising defeat against AS Monaco at Tynecastle.

Hearts’ hopes of reaching the knockout stage rest on winning their last two Conference League matches against Bosnian side Borac Banja Luca and Cypriot team Pafos, probably by high-scoring margins.

Did you know with a Digital Subscription to The Scotsman, you can get unlimited access to the website including our premium content, as well as benefiting from fewer ads, loyalty rewards and much more.

The Tynecastle manager was not giving up on anything after the 3-2 loss, with United States World Cup star Folarin Balogun scoring the winning goal in the final seconds of added time.

Sources indicate that hearts had taken the lead after a sensational strike from Jordi Altena on 15 minutes. A penalty from Balogun levelled things before the visitors took the lead with a goal from Edam Diop five minutes before half time. Sabah Kerjota scored the goal of the night on the stroke of half-time after curling in with his left foot to leave everything to play for in the second half.

Industry observers note that “I think the point doesn't make a difference,” remarked Vrancken. “There's also something that really was pleasing for me is that when it was 2-2, we still wanted to go (for the win).

"You saw also when it was a throw-in, we wanted to do it fast, we wanted to go for the win. Against a side like this, in the situation we're in, I am so really proud of this also.

Recent findings suggest that "Three points would make a difference," he added. "Zero or one point doesn't make a difference towards the next games, so you have to win the next games. One point or no points doesn't change anything in the next games.”.

According to recent reports, the Belgian stressed his pride in his players and reiterated that Hearts were missing nine injured players as well as Leart Kabashi and Eduardo Ageu, who were not named in the European squad. He did, however, lament the lack of concentration that saw them concede so late in the game after 93-and-a-half minutes of lung-busting effort. He was also unhappy that Hearts were not cute enough to stop Monaco in their tracks as they broke free for the winning goal. Substitute Finlay Pollock had the chance to clip Mamadou Coulibaly’s heels before the midfielder played in Balogun. Ruthlessness might be something Hearts are lacking at this level. A reporter pointed out that it was a cruel way to lose a match.

Sources indicate that “It did feel like this,” mentioned Vrancken. “But at the same time, we have to learn in that situation because I think until then we were really solid about giving chances away. And I expect more from guys who come in from the side (substitutes).

Industry observers note that “We can win it with a fresh player and in the middle we can win it with a fresh player. Or you make a foul somewhere to keep the result - I expect this. This is like battling for the team, as I call it.

Recent findings suggest that “We have to do better there,” he added. “But the biggest thing, of course, is to be really proud of what performance we put on the park today, because it's against a really good side. Knowing that we have still nine injuries - I will name it - and we have a lot of players not on the European list today and still do this against that team. I'm really proud of what we did.”.

Recent findings suggest that he hailed the quality of his side’s goals. “You see also the confidence those guys have. This is what we wanted after the weekend, of course - that you take some confidence from the dynamics of what we did there. I think the conviction around the box was there, in both boxes actually. It's an notable thing to take with us towards the next games coming, especially in this run of games.”.

Hearts host Celtic, who beat them 7-1 last month, at Tynecastle on Sunday. Vrancken is firmly in the belief that his side have their mojo back following this and the 5-2 defeat to Falkirk earlier this month. Hearts have since beaten Dundee 8-0 and been edged out by Monaco in a five-goal thriller. “We have played two good games and two good performances against good sides, especially today,” he noted. “And now you have the confidence. But we are still playing against a good side on Sunday with only two days' rest, so we have to manage fatigue and make sure that we are as fresh as possible again to make up for something a few weeks ago, especially because it's an at-home game.”.

Monaco manager Filipe Luis, meanwhile, denied that relief was the primary emotion after leaving it so late to collect three points. “It is not relief, we compete to win,” he remarked. “We had an amazing opportunity to win tonight but we had a tough opponent.

Recent findings suggest that “They scored two unbelievable goals,” he added. “You almost need to applaud them. When a team scores two goals like this it is almost nobody’s fault. They are two fantastic goals. Honestly, it’s very beautiful.”.

He spoke admiringly of the atmosphere. “I played against Celtic (with Atletico Madrid) in 2011 I think in the Europa League,” he mentioned. “We are lucky to have the opportunity to play these types of games in different countries. It is so intense. I am happy to have had this opportunity to be here tonight – and happy with the result.”.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Colombian’s late header ends Celtic’s 23-year Portuguese hoodoo in gritty Torreense triumph.

Celtic clinched a vital 2-1 Europa League victory over second-tier outfit Torreense, thanks to an 84th-minute header from substitute Camilo Duran that ended the Scottish champions' 23-and-a-half-year wait for an away win on Portuguese soil.

Industry observers note that played nearly 50 miles away from Torreense’s 2,431-capacity home at Estadio Manuel Marques, which fails to meet UEFA stadium criteria, the 24,000-seater Municipal Stadium in Leiria was dominated by roughly 4,000 travelling Celtic supporters, making up two-thirds of the crowd. Despite the partisan backing, Martin O’Neill’s men made remarkably hard work of overcoming a side sitting 13th in Portugal’s second division with just two league wins from their opening ten matches.

There is an old adage in European football that fortunes earned by accident are rarely retained by design. For 45 disjointed minutes, Celtic offered a textbook demonstration of the principle. Handed an early advantage through the sort of comical defending usually reserved for Scottish clubs on their continental travels, Martin O’Neill’s side promptly retreated into their shell, allowing Portuguese second-tier minnows Torreense to restore parity and seize the initiative before the interval.

It has been revealed that celtic’s precarious Europa League campaign was balanced on a knife-edge. Having opened their league-phase campaign with three consecutive defeats before salvaging a breathless 3-2 victory over Beşiktaş in Glasgow earlier this month, O’Neill’s men arrived in central Portugal languishing in 32nd place.

Anything less than maximum points against a Torreense side operating in the lower reaches of Liga Portugal 2, yet remarkably seated 19th in this competition with six points following last season’s improbable Taça de Portugal triumph, threatened to render Celtic’s remaining fixtures against Omonia, Marseille, and Union Saint-Gilloise an exercise in mathematical futility.

Sources indicate that O’Neill had cautioned on the eve of the tie that his squad lacked the pedigree to indulge in complacency. Initially, however, the evening appeared set to unfold with uncharacteristic smoothness for the Scottish champions.

Restored to the European squad as an injury replacement for Mika Baur, Jota marked his return to his homeland with immediate industry down the left flank. Inside nine minutes, the winger collected possession near the by-line and whipped a low, enticing delivery into the six-yard box. With Yang Hyun-jun hovering intently at the back post, Torreense full-back Javi Vázquez panicked under pressure, slicing his attempted clearance past his own goalkeeper and into the net.

It was a moment of extreme generosity, yet Celtic proved remarkably ungrateful recipients. Rather than using their early cushion to assert authority, the visitors lapsed into a passive, defensive shell. Though Celtic commanded the majority of possession, they managed to invite pressure rather than alleviate it.

Torreense, a club steeped in modest provincial history rather than continental glamour, sensed the vulnerability. Vázquez nearly atoned for his earlier mistake in the 17th minute with a venomous, low free-kick from a narrow angle that required hasty defensive intervention. Two minutes later, the equaliser duly arrived, born of Celtic’s chronic inability to clear their lines.

Given acres of space 20 yards from goal, midfielder Álex Alfaro unleashed a fierce drive that crashed against the underside of Sam Johnstone’s crossbar. As the ball dropped invitingly inside the penalty area, Celtic’s backline froze. Kieran Tierney’s tentative, lofted clearance succeeded only in teeing up Dany Jean, and the forward exhibited admirable composure to dart past Colby Donovan and drill a low finish beyond Johnstone’s reach.

Industry observers note that jota remained Celtic’s sole reliable source of invention. Celtic’s solitary threat to reclaim the lead prior to the break arrived on the stroke of half-time, when the Portuguese star's deep cross was hooked back across the face of goal by Luke McCowan, only for Kasper Høgh to arrive a fraction too late to apply the finishing touch.

Recent findings suggest that jota nearly restored the lead within seconds of the restart, only for his attempted dink to be gathered by a scrambling Adriel. But as the hour mark approached, Celtic’s frustration grew.

Former Hearts striker Musa Drammeh nearly dealt a massive blow to their hopes of progressing to the knockout stages by shrugging off a feeble challenge before dragging a golden chance narrowly wide of the far post.

Sources indicate that james Forrest took over from the impressive Jota in the closing stages and the substitution proved to be a masterstroke. With Celtic seemingly sleepwalking toward a damaging result, Forrest swung a pinpoint cross in from the right, and Duran peeled away at the back post to power a downward header past Adriel. It was the Colombian’s 15th goal of a remarkable campaign, once again rescuing his side.

In a recent development, mcCowan missed a late one-on-one opportunity to add a touch of gloss to the scoreline in the 89th minute, seeing his tame finish saved by Adriel’s boot. However, it did not matter. For the first time since O’Neill’s side triumphed at Boavista in April 2003, Celtic left Iberian soil victorious.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By Ellis Stevens | 26 Nov 2026 14:21.

The Scottish Premiership's second and third-placed sides will meet on Saturday, when Rangers welcome Falkirk to Ibrox Stadium.

The hosts are second in the Scottish Premiership standings with 33 points, one point behind leaders Celtic, while the visitors are third with 24 points from 14 matches.

Rangers head into Saturday's match with their sights set on moving to the top of the Scottish Premiership standings for the first time this season.

The Gers trail leaders Celtic by just one point, meaning a victory would lift them above their Old Firm rivals, at least until the Bhoys take on Hearts on Sunday afternoon.

Derek McInnes' men will be full of confidence of claiming all three points, with Rangers heading into the matchday 15 fixture enjoying a sensational 14-game unbeaten run across all competitions.

In the league, Rangers have won 10 and drawn two matches during that run, including winning each of their last three Scottish Premiership fixtures, beating St Mirren 2-0, Motherwell 2-1 and Aberdeen 3-2.

The Gers are also looking to extend their superb record at Ibrox, having won all of their last nine home games, scoring 22 and conceding just four goals in that time.

Despite their fantastic form coming into this match, Rangers will expect a tough test against visitors Falkirk, who travel to Ibrox off the back of six consecutive league triumphs.

That run includes particularly notable wins against Celtic (2-0) and Hearts (5-2), and the Bairns will now be looking to add Rangers' scalp to their collection.

Thanks to those six victories, Falkirk have rapidly ascended to third in the Scottish Premiership standings with 24 points from 14 matches, although they only lead Hearts - who have played one game fewer - by one point.

Alongside their impressive recent run, Falkirk will draw further self belief from their formidable record on the road this season, recording three wins, three draws and suffering just one loss away from home in the league.

John McGlynn's side have, however, failed to defeat Rangers in any of their last seven encounters, including a 2-1 defeat earlier this season.

Rangers form (all competitions):.

Falkirk Scottish Premiership form:.

Rangers are set to be without Cameron Devlin, Daisuke Yokota, Jose Cifuentes, Lawrence Shankland and Youssef Chermiti due to ongoing injuries, while Ross McCrorie is also a doubt with a hamstring injury.

Ryan Don Naderi is Rangers' top scorer in the league with seven goals, and the forward should continue just behind Kevin Kelsy in the forward line.

Falkirk are also contending with several injury absences, including Aidan Nesbitt, Aodhan Doherty, Brad Spencer, Leon McCann and Ryan Strain, while Ethan Laidlaw is a doubt to feature.

Jacob Murrell is Falkirk's top scorer with eight league goals, including seven in his last seven appearances, and the forward will start just ahead of Ethan Ross, Finley Barbrook and Owen Eames in attack.

Rangers possible starting lineup:.

Pandur; Sterling, Fernandez, Makhanya, Penrice; Raskin, Neil; Bouanani, Naderi, Gassama; Kelsy.

Falkirk possible starting lineup:.

Bain; McMillan, Neilson, Henderson, Tanser; Krauhaus, Melniks; Ross, Barbrook, Eames; Murrell.

Both teams head into this match in fantastic form, leading us to expect a hard-fought encounter. However, given Rangers' formidable Ibrox form and their recent upperhand in this fixture, we are predicting a victory for the hosts.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

When Manchester City play like this what a loss their football will be to the Premier League – and the Champions League – if they are heavily sanctioned later this season.

In what turned out to be a match for the ages, a night of brilliant, unbridled attack, we were treated to the ultimate game of two halves as the back-to-back European champions Paris St-Germain took City apart for 45 minutes. And then were left holding on.

City will hope this is a sign of what is to come in their Premier League fight. But with a different result. After suffering a resounding defeat at the hands of the Premier League’s independent commission, with 114 of the 115 charges against them proven, they maintain their innocence and are mounting an appeal.

Could they make a comeback? It would be incredible and highly improbable if they did so but, out on the pitch, and 3-0 down after a first half in which they were in danger of being humiliated by PSG, they created enough opportunities to save themselves.

The data backed that. City’s expected goals (xG) was 2.57 while PSG’s was 1.83. City had 27 shots to 15 and had more possession and more passes. Enzo Maresca made a triple substitution to devastating effect, especially with the introduction of new signings Ayyoub Bouaddi and Iliman Ndiaye.

In the end they clawed back two goals, both scored by Erling Haaland, who now has 61 in 60 games in this competition – seventh outright in the all-time list, before Ruud van Nistelrooy. And 37 of those for City, overtaking Sergio Agüero’s club record.

Erling Haaland gets his second of the night, and the game could be back on 🔥 📺 Stream on TNT Sports & HBO Max https://t.co/sFZ0eT2Egz.

According to recent reports, “Even with 3-0 in the first half, with the amount of chances we created in the second half, we deserved more. Luis [Enrique, PSG’s coach] said at the end of the game that they were quite lucky,” Maresca claimed before being asked whether he would relish facing PSG again, later in this competition. “My feeling is we are there. We are close,” he added.

Recent findings suggest that did City deserve a draw? No one was predicting that at half-time as they were suffering as comprehensive a defeat as was inflicted by the commission. Accused of “sham” contracts to inflate income, this was a sham of a performance, made all the more emphatic because of how brilliant PSG, and their exceptional 21-year-old winger Désiré Doué, were.

It was a meeting of two clubs empowered more than any other by the riches of Gulf states: Abu Dhabi versus Qatar. Both have also had their run-ins over money. Both were sanctioned, but escaped full bans by Uefa for breaching financial fair play rules.

The question, also, was: would the eighth meeting of these clubs in the Champions League in the last 11 seasons be the last for some time?

Crawley extended their unbeaten run in the league under Blackwell to four games with a 0-0 draw at home to title contenders Barnet in midweek – and Blackwell now believes that his side are “competitive” – not only on the eye but also according to the data.

The former Sheffield United manager stated: “The data shows that we're very competitive now with sprints, decelerations, accelerations, high-speed runs. We're now coming at the top half of the table with that so it just shows that we've been improving all over.”.

Did you know with an ad-lite subscription to SussexWorld, you get 70% fewer ads while viewing the news that matters to you.

From a defensive point of view the past two games have shown a rejuvenated back-line – helped by the recent additions of Ben Heneghan and Josh Flint, which have made the Reds look a lot more resolute and solid.

Exeter are right now one spot below the play-off places sitting in 8th place on 23 points. The Grecians have the best defensive record in the league having only conceded 10 goals but Blackwell is not fazed by that.

He has communicated as much to his players: “It doesn't matter whether they're the top or the bottom, we feel now that we can compete with people, and that's all I wanted to do, make us competitive. Then hopefully Lady Luck smiles on you on the day and you can get some good results.”.

Blackwell was pleased that more players have stepped up to the mark to give him more confidence in choices.

In a recent development, he said: “We talk about how any team wants to be competitive from 1-22 really, and know that if you lose a player, that someone can seamlessly step in. What was pleasing was that we made some changes, shifted it around a little bit, and then whoever we brought in did a good job, so that gives me more power.”.

With the Reds involved in a lunchtime kick-off, Blackwell was asked whether that makes a difference to the way they approach the game.

He replied: “I think it's something that I've been used to now for the last 15 years, you know, being in a Championship or the Premier League and abroad in Poland is exactly the same.

“You don't know whether you're playing a Friday, a Saturday, a Sunday or a Monday, they're the four days that you normally play.

“You don't know whether you're going to be at 12 o'clock, 2pm, 4pm, 8pm – so it's now it's just normal for players; it certainly has been for me. So nothing different, whatever the time is, we'll prepare as if it were a 3pm kick-off or a 1pm kick-off. Preparation is the same.”.

Jota’s cross led to the opening goal and the Portuguese winger was Celtic’s brightest player before going off just before the hour mark on his first European appearance since the Hoops came within seconds of beating Bayern Munich in Germany in February 2025.

“He did superbly well,” O’Neill said. “He’s getting fitter each game he plays. That’s the longest he’s lasted so far and he did really well.

Forrest drew level with Scott Brown’s Celtic record of 127 European appearances.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • By Matt Law | 26 Nov 2026 14:44, Last updated: 26 Nov 2026 20:20.
  • Real Madrid will be aiming to make it 11 straight wins in all competitions when they welcome Alaves to Bernabeu on Saturday night.
  • Los Blancos have been victorious in each of their last nine games against Alaves, including a 2-1 victory in the corresponding match during the 2025-26 campaign.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By Matt Law | 26 Nov 2026 14:44, Last updated: 26 Nov 2026 20:20.

Real Madrid will be aiming to make it 11 straight wins in all competitions when they welcome Alaves to Bernabeu on Saturday night.

Los Blancos have been victorious in each of their last nine games against Alaves, including a 2-1 victory in the corresponding match during the 2025-26 campaign.

Real Madrid will enter this weekend's match off the back of a 5-1 win over PSV Eindhoven in the Champions League, with that success making it 10 victories in a row in all competitions.

Jose Mourinho's side are flying, with their winning run including six in Spain's top flight, and they are at the moment second in the La Liga table, only three points off the leaders Barcelona.

Los Blancos now have three straight league matches against Alaves, Real Sociedad and Athletic Bilbao before resuming their Champions League campaign away to Arsenal on December 9.

Real Madrid would go level on points with Barcelona should they manage to win this match, and they have been victorious in 38 of their previous 46 games against Alaves in all competitions, suffering only five defeats in the process.

Vinicius Junior is still finding it difficult to show his best form for Real Madrid, but Kylian Mbappe is having another incredible campaign, netting 19 times in 18 appearances in all competitions.

Alaves will be the huge underdogs this weekend, but two of their last three wins over Real Madrid have come away from home, including a 2-1 success at Bernabeu in November 2020.

The Blue and Whites will enter this match off the back of a 3-1 win over Deportivo La Coruna, with the result leaving them in ninth spot in the La Liga table on 16 points, boasting a record of four wins, four draws and five defeats from their 13 matches.

Quique Sanchez Flores's side have been excellent at home this season, picking up 13 points from seven matches, but they are still waiting for their first away success of the campaign.

Alaves finished 14th in Spain's top flight last season, only one point above the relegation zone, so there is clear room for improvement in 2026-27.

The Basque outfit will be the fresher of the two teams following Real Madrid's Champions League involvement, but they will be up against a side that have the second-best defensive record (11 conceded) and second-best attacking record (33 scored) during the current season.

Real Madrid form (all competitions):.

Alaves form (all competitions):.

Real Madrid will be missing Rodrygo (knee), Raul Asencio (leg), Ferland Mendy (hip) and Endrick (groin) through injury on Saturday, but no fresh issues have been reported.

There will be changes to the side that took to the field for the first whistle against PSV, with Denzel Dumfries, Ibrahima Konate and Dean Huijsen potentially all being introduced into the defence.

Jude Bellingham should also return to the starting side, with Yan Diomande potentially being rested from the first whistle to allow Arda Guler and Vinicius Junior to feature in the wide areas.

As for Alaves, Facundo Garces (knee), Mikel Rodriguez (knee) and Hugo Noava (muscle) are unavailable.

Given the nature of the result and indeed the performance against Deportivo last time out, it is possible that it could be same again in terms of the starting team for the visitors.

Lucas Boye has scored six times in 12 appearances this season, and the 30-year-old is again set to feature in the final third, while Denis Suarez and Antonio Blanco are also set to be in the XI.

Real Madrid possible starting lineup:.

Courtois; Dumfries, Konate, Huijsen, Cucurella; Valverde, Tchouameni; Guler, Bellingham, Vinicius; Mbappe.

Alaves possible starting lineup:.

Sivera; Tenaglia, Koski, Otto; Perez, Ibanez, Blanco, Suarez, Rebbach; Martinez, Boye.

Alaves deserve credit for what has been a solid season to date, but Real Madrid are in a good place at the moment, and we are fully expecting Mourinho's side to claim another three points.

  • Manchester United have hit out at referees’ boss Howard Webb after winning an appeal to have Leny Yoro’s red card at Liverpool overturned.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By CHRIS WHEELER, NORTHERN SPORTS WRITER.

Published: 10:23 EST, 24 November 2026 | Updated: 02:10 EST, 25 November 2026.

Manchester United have hit out at referees’ boss Howard Webb after winning an appeal to have Leny Yoro’s red card at Liverpool overturned.

An FA independent regulatory commission on Tuesday ruled that Yoro was wrongfully dismissed by referee Sam Barrott at Anfield on Sunday as United’s 10 men suffered a 4-0 defeat in Mauricio Pochettino’s first game in charge.

It has been revealed that but United are furious that Pro Ref boss Webb has refused to admit the error after he backed Barrott’s decision and VAR’s refusal to overturn it on the Mic’d Up show on Sky Sports. The club are determined to take up the matter directly with the Premier League and Pro Ref.

Yoro was sent off for pushing Alexander Isak in the back, but United disputed the referee’s view that the Liverpool striker would have got to the ball before goalkeeper Senne Lammens.

The FA panel appeared to agree as it rescinded Yoro’s red card and lifted his one-match ban on the basis that he did not deny Isak an obvious goalscoring opportunity – meaning the Frenchman can play against Brentford at Old Trafford on Saturday.

According to recent reports, however, Webb argued: ‘That was the referee’s call, made on the field. Then the VAR checks whether the decision made on the field was clearly and obviously incorrect – and formed the opinion it wasn’t.

Leny Yoro has seen his red card suspension overturned following an appeal by Man United.

Pro Ref boss Howard Webb believed it was the right decision for Yoro to be sent off on Sunday.

Recent findings suggest that ‘I think by and large, most people would see that as a correct decision, with Isak moving quickly on towards that ball. The alternative view is that Lammens might get there first, but I think it's a little bit debatable, I guess. Certainly not clearly wrong.’.

United sources have branded this interpretation as ‘totally wrong’ and say it is a process error that fails to interpret the rules properly. They believe that the VAR audio proves there was no meaningful consideration given to challenging Barrott’s decision.

United dispute that it was subjective call and say that it can be proved objectively in a matter of minutes using data that Isak could not have reached the ball before Lammens, even at top speed.

Pochettino blamed the decision for United’s defeat at Anfield, and took aim at VAR again after landing in Portugal last night (tues) for the Champions League tie against Sporting Lisbon.

‘I’m very disappointed because I think this kind of thing never can happen,’ noted Pochettino, who also felt that Dominik Szoboszlai’s opening goal from the resulting free kick should have been disallowed because Bradley Barcola made contact with United’s defensive wall.

‘The referee can make a mistake but if we have VAR what were they doing? We need to take time to review the situation.’.

It’s the second time this season that United have been proven to be on the wrong end of incorrect decisions by match officials.

In September, Webb apologised to United after Erling Haaland’s winning goal for Manchester City in the Old Trafford derby was allowed to stand.

Tonight’s (wed) game sees United captain Bruno Fernandes face his old team Sporting amid increasing uncertainty over his future at Old Trafford after talks over a new contact stalled.

According to recent reports, ‘We have time to speak about that,’ said Fernandes. ‘I know it's my future and I probably shouldn't look that way because I haven't got long left, but I'm more worried about results.’.

Asked if he would consider a return to Sporting, who sold him to United for £68million in 2020, Fernandes added: ‘I will never close the door to Sporting. It will always be a club with a special place in my heart.’.

The former Aston Villa and Everton midfielder's Hull season had been a slow burner after joining with an abductor injury picked up in the summer which severely limited his pre-season, but he was just starting to find some form.

His four starts for the club have all come in the last four games.

Sources indicate that hull Live are reporting he could miss three months at the time of year when the Premier League calendar is at its most condensed, with UEFA's cup competitions set for a winter break. That period could include 16 of Hull's 38 league matches.
