Ahead of a do-or-die clash against Olympiacos for AC Milan in the Europa League, Ruben Amorim spoke to the media.

There’s still time for Milan to turn around their Europa League campaign, but so far, it’s been one to forget. Their successes in the league have often been reduced thanks to poor performances in midweek, and that cannot happen again.

Recent findings suggest that read SempreMilan ad-free and get access to exclusive news. Click here for a free trial!

After a dismantling of Frosinone at the weekend, Amorim’s side should be full of confidence and wholesale rotations are not expected in Greece tomorrow night. So, logically, that confidence should continue and there should be several reasons to feel hopeful of a result.

In a recent development, however, as we know, there have been similar feelings heading into Europe this season and the Rossoneri have often not followed up with performances of similar levels. Tomorrow must be different.

Speaking alongside Ardon Jashari, the Portuguese discussed the challenge his team will face tomorrow, as MilanNews relays.

What do you ask of the team for tomorrow? More volume in attack? How do you plan to support Ramos?

“It’s not about helping Ramos, but also Camarda and everyone up front. It’s a fact that we need to improve in the final third. The only thing we can do is improve our principles. We need to improve on these little things, and that’s the only way I can help my players.

“Against Olympiacos, it will be a different match than the one against Frosinone, just as it will be different than the one against Cagliari.

In a recent development, “We need to improve, even in our defending. We’ve almost always conceded a goal, so that’s another area we need to improve.”.

How would you describe Olympiacos as a team?

Sources indicate that “Thank you for the welcome. They’re a strong team. They’re aggressive, especially at home. I’ve played here twice, and it was tough for me. I know their coach and what he wants to do.

“They play compact, positive football, 4-3-3; they change a lot, they rotate, they have Jota, a lot of Portuguese players. They’re a strong team, and with their fans there, it’ll be a tough match.

“Chiquinho is a great talent, but very impulsive. I hope he plays well tomorrow, but I hope he still has a great career ahead of him.”.

Does AC Milan’s growth also involve Europe?

“To be a good team, you have to do well both in the league and in Europe. That’s the only way to be a good team. We have to be, especially at Milan.

It has been revealed that “My compliments? I’m always waiting for things to go badly, because it doesn’t take much to change the situation. That’s what I’m trying to make my players understand, because it won’t always be this way.

“We’re at the beginning of a process, and I think we need everyone. We lost Pavlovic, Modric, Saelemaekers, Chukwueze, and everyone has to be ready, because there are no excuses at significant clubs. We have to be ready for this.

Recent findings suggest that “I can’t believe we lost all these games in Europe because we rotated. We have to always be ready and approach the games like against Inter, Frosinone, and Genoa. We’re building so many things. Tomorrow is another test for us.

According to recent reports, “I believe in all competitions, but if we can win them all, no. Scudetto? I haven’t changed my mind. This year is difficult, but if we have the chance to fight, we’ll do it. I won’t change for the compliments, because I’m waiting and so are you.

“You’re waiting [for criticism]. Tomorrow we have to win, because if we don’t… I’m ready for that.”.

Is football becoming dangerous for the mental and physical health of players and coaches?

According to recent reports, “It’s difficult to protect players considering the times we’re living in. Younger players will be more willing to live with criticism. It’s different from my reality. It’s difficult to control this.

“When you asked me about GTA, I’d rather my players play every day rather than scroll through social media. What I mean is that we want more time between games. I’m talking about the product, not my life.

“I’m talking about the quality of the football product. I don’t know what Fabregas meant, but it’s the evolution of society, of football, which is a business, and we have to be ready.

Sources indicate that “Social media, and all that stuff, is very difficult for players, who in any case live with more criticism than I do. After Frosinone, I haven’t read anything, because that’s how I want to live my life.”.

You have a lot of experience as a player: what do you expect from the stadium tomorrow?

“I know the atmosphere here. It’s incredible. It’s important for my players to have this experience, even though there’s no stadium more difficult to play in than San Siro. We have to be ready in these kinds of stadiums.

According to recent reports, “We lost 5-1 once, but I’m very focused on what we have to do, how we’ll start the match, I’m focused on these things. The atmosphere should be normal for these players, who are used to substantial events. We have to be competitive and ready.”.

Town, who needed to win to go level on points at the top with League One leaders Stockport County, eased to a 2-0 lead inside 21 minutes, thanks to strikes from Cameron Humphrys - his first of the campaign - and top-scorer Joe Taylor.

But Bali Mumba's second dismissal of the season - a second yellow card for hauling down Jamie Sterry on 34 minutes - gave Rovers hope with Isaac Hutchinson scoring from the resultant penalty.

But despite being a man light, the visitors produced an organised and controlled second half and managed to add a killer third just before the hour mark, courtesy of Ilias Bronkhorst.

Home captain Owen Bailey pulled one back in stoppage-time, but Town held out for a deserved triumph, their first ever in the league at this venue and following up their win in the Trophy at the Club Doncaster Sports Village at the start of September.

Drury remarked: “I thought we started the game really well and I really liked the way that the players showed real courage and belief early doors with the ball.

"I felt we competed really well in duels in moments where we had to be good because of the energy that Doncaster have and to score two goals early on, I felt we were in real control of the game at that point.

"We obviously then have the sending off.

In a recent development, "These things happen in football, so we have to respond from that. We're down to 10 men and it's about not just managing the game, but managing certain moments within the game.

"I thought the players were excellent, I thought they were outstanding.

"We had to defend some substantial moments towards the end of the game. We tried to get the subs right in terms of not just personnel, but actually size of people coming on in context to what the game might throw at us.

"Obviously, later on, you're expecting more set plays, more crosses into the box from the opponent, which is why we waited on that and got some more height on towards the end of the game.

Sources indicate that "I think the credit for tonight has to go solely to the players on the pitch. For everyone that started the game, everyone that came on and everyone that's been involved around it, I thought it was a real well-connected team effort tonight.".

On the dismissal of Mumba, who received his marching orders for the second time this term, he added: "I look at the last few games, Bali saved us two or three times in the last few games from those types of recovery runs.

"Tonight, we just got one wrong in terms of our timing and when he tried to win the ball.

Industry observers note that "These things happen in football. It's not something we're happy about, but it's not something that I'm going to start criticising. It's just something for us to work on and get better at.".

One significant downer on the night arrived with the news that midfielder Archie Collins come off in the second half with a hamstring injury.

McCann commented: "He doesn't look too good. He doesn't look too good.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • By Ben Sully | 26 Nov 2026 15:22.
  • Wrexham will look to extend their four-game unbeaten run when they welcome Portsmouth to the Racecourse Ground for Saturday’s Championship encounter.
  • Pompey, meanwhile, will be eyeing a second straight win after getting the better of West Ham United in midweek.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By Ben Sully | 26 Nov 2026 15:22.

Wrexham will look to extend their four-game unbeaten run when they welcome Portsmouth to the Racecourse Ground for Saturday’s Championship encounter.

Pompey, meanwhile, will be eyeing a second straight win after getting the better of West Ham United in midweek.

After overseeing just three wins in the first 13 league games, Wrexham boss Phil Parkinson has eased some of the pressure that was building on his shoulders with a four-game unbeaten run.

Wrexham went into the international window on the back of a 2-0 win over Middlesbrough and a 1-1 draw against Wolverhampton Wanderers, before they returned to action with a narrow 1-0 victory over Lincoln City at Sincil Bank.

They then took the lead in Tuesday’s away clash with Bristol City, but were ultimately forced to settle for a point after Joe Worrall saw his opener cancelled out by Cam Pring’s equaliser, leaving Wrexham in 14th spot in the Championship table and five points adrift of the top eight.

After playing back-to-back away games, Wrexham will be looking forward to returning to the familiar surroundings of the Racecourse Ground, where they have taken seven points from their last three outings since losing to West Bromwich Albion last month.

Wrexham are also one of six teams to score in every Championship home match this term, extending their overall run to at least one goal in each of their last 15 home league games since drawing a blank in a 2-0 loss to Millwall over seven months ago.

In fact, that scoring run includes a 2-1 victory in their recent meeting with Portsmouth in February, which came courtesy of first-half goals from Sam Smith and Max Cleworth.

Portsmouth, meanwhile, are just two points adrift of the playoffs after winning five, drawing three and losing just one of their last nine matches.

After losing to Stoke City before the international window, Pompey resumed their campaign with a hard-fought away draw against Bolton Wanderers before they claimed a 1-0 win in their first home meeting with West Ham United in 14 years.

Odin Bailey’s maiden Portsmouth goal proved enough to secure the club’s first head-to-head victory since a 1-0 success at Upton Park in April 2008, while also keeping their first home clean sheet since the start of September.

John Mousinho’s side will now head on their travels with hopes of extending their four-game unbeaten away run, which started with a 1-0 win over Norwich City and continued with three consecutive draws on the road.

No Championship team has conceded fewer away goals than Portsmouth, whose defence has been breached just six times in their eight road trips this season.

Given the fact they only took a point from their two meetings with Wrexham last term, Pompey will head into Saturday's fixture with hopes of claiming their first head-to-head league win since recording a 2-0 away victory in January 1983.

Wrexham forward Sam Smith will miss the remainder of the season after sustaining an anterior cruciate ligament injury earlier this month.

The hosts are also likely to be without the services of Liberato Cacace, Seb Revan, Josh Windass, Callum O’Hare and Nathan Broadhead.

Ollie Rathbone and Kieffer Moore are pushing for starting berths, the latter of whom is Wrexham’s top scorer with five Championship goals to his name this term.

Jayden Meghoma will be out for up to 10 weeks after sustaining an ankle ligament injury in last weekend’s draw against Bolton.

Meghoma is the latest addition to a lengthy injury list that features Keshi Anderson, Luke Brooke-Smith, Marko Milovanovic, Colby Bishop, John Swift, Mark Kosznovszky, Connor Ogilvie and Benjamin Arthur.

Marlon Pack, Josh Murphy and Adrian Segecic are options to start if Mousinho decides to freshen up his side for Saturday’s away trip.

Wrexham possible starting lineup:.

Patterson; Cleworth, Worrall, Doyle; Kabore, Dobson, Whiteman, Ekomie; O’Brien, Rathbone; Moore.

Portsmouth possible starting lineup:.

Schmid; Devlin, Poole, Dia, Swanson; Pack, Mohamed; Segecic, Bailey, Murphy; Shade.

Portsmouth have conceded more than one goal in just one of their eight away league games this term, and with that in mind, we think they will do enough to avoid defeat in Saturday's fixture.

However, we believe they will fall short of claiming maximum points against a Wrexham side that are unbeaten in four games.

Despite playing with an extra man for an hour following the 34th-minute dismissal of Bali Mumba, which enabled Isaac Hutchinson to reduce the arrears for a Rovers side trailing 2-0 after 21 minutes through goals from Cameron Humphreys and Joe Taylor, the hosts still flattered to deceive.

Ilias Bronkhorst grabbed a killer third for Town, who moved joint top, just before the hour mark and despite captain Owen Bailey pulling one back for Rovers late on, it was to no avail.

Did you know with a Digital subscription to Yorkshire Post, you can get access to all of our premium content, as well as benefiting from fewer ads, loyalty rewards and much more.

Doncaster remain in the bottom four of League One, having won just once in their last seven outings. During the run, they have shipped 18 goals.

McCann mentioned: "I felt we started the game really badly and the two goals we conceded in the first half were so disappointing from our point of view.

"We had enough bodies around the ball for both goals, we switch off on the run, the midfield player makes a run into the box and we don't see him.

"With the second one, we had enough bodies around the ball and we didn't get in a position to block the shot from Joe Taylor. Then we got a bit of a lifeline, having started the game so poorly, it was a really good move to get the penalty and they went down to 10 men and Hutch is calm from the spot.

"The message at half time is to go and win the game, a real opportunity to win the game at home, with Huddersfield down to 10 men, but we just huffed and puffed, we didn't show enough quality.

"We didn't create enough overloads in the wide areas which was a plan at half time, we kept coming inside and when you give a team like a transition team like Huddersfield the opportunity they give on a break and we concede a set-play which is really disappointing with four players around three and then we go on and we get done with it.

"That gives us a bigger challenge, just the lack of quality from an attacking point of view and the poor defensive goals that we conceded has done us.

"They've got top quality players, the front three are probably the best three in the division and so quick on the transition, they've got a bit of everything—they've got pace, they've got physicality and athleticism.

In a recent development, "But it's really disappointing, I don't think they've had to do a lot to score those goals and that's the most frustrating thing about it. We've played against Huddersfield and Bradford in the last two games and scored four goals and you're thinking that's enough to get you more than one point, it's not.

"We've conceded five sloppy goals in the last couple of games and that's the reason why we've only got one point from it.".

Joao Pedro has visited his former club Watford as he nurses a thigh injury that is keeping him out of the Chelsea team.

The Brazilian was Chelsea’s most notable player last season and began this season in fine form, scoring five times and assisting a further three goals in the Blues’ opening six games of the campaign.

But the 25-year-old has been out since sustaining a thigh injury on the eve of last month’s 2-0 home defeat to Tottenham.

On Wednesday, during his recovery period, Joao Pedro visited the club where it all began for him in English football as he returned to Vicarage Road.

He and his girlfriend Khadije were special guests as Watford hosted Blackburn in the Championship.

Sources indicate that on their social media channels, Watford welcomed the striker back to his former home, writing: “The boy from Brazil is back in town. Great to see you, Joao.”.

The result did not go the way the Chelsea striker would have wanted, as the Hornets were beaten 1-0 with their incoming manager Edward Iordanescu watching on from the stands.

Joao Pedro made 109 appearances for Watford between 2020 and 2023 before signing for Brighton.

After spending just two seasons on the south coast with the Seagulls, he joined Chelsea in July 2025 for a fee of £55million rising to £60m inclusive of add-ons.

Your weekly briefing on Tottenham, featuring team news and expert analysis from Sam Tabuteau.

Industry observers note that I would like to be emailed about offers, event and updates from Evening Standard. Read our privacy notice.

Teenage defender Isaac Allen has confirmed that he has joined Tottenham after leaving rivals West Ham in the summer.

In August, reports claimed that Spurs had beaten Arsenal to Allen’s signature, and the 15-year-old has now unveiled the move on social media.

The England U15s captain wrote in a post on Instagram: “Happy to be signed with Tottenham.”.

Allen, who can operate either at centre-back or in defensive midfield, is regarded as one of the most promising young talents in England and his arrival continues Spurs’ busy youth recruitment strategy.

During last month’s Fan Advisory Board (FAB) meeting, the club confirmed that as part of their commitment to the academy, they had actively recruited players aged 16 and under and invested in the U10 to U17 age groups.

Allen is the latest highly-rated teenage talent to arrive at Hotspur Way, with Cole Ramsey (19), Kwasi Senyah (16), Gabriel Rigg (15) and Jake Maloney (14) all signing in recent months.

Tottenham are understood to be pairing football development with private schooling and strong professional terms once players turn 17, to beat competition from rival clubs.

The change in approach has been brought on by an acknowledgement internally that Spurs have struggled not only to offer academy players a pathway into the first team, but also to maximise their value by selling them on if they don’t believe they have a future at the club.

Tottenham hope to highlight the progression of 18-year-old winger Luca Williams-Barnett, who scored and assisted on his full senior debut in the Premier League against Ipswich last weekend before being handed a new long-term contract, as an example of the pathway into the first team.

Meanwhile, the success of the current Championship leading goalscorer Will Lankshear, who joined Middlesbrough in a deal worth up to £20million in the summer, showcases Spurs’ willingness to find productive permanent solutions for players who can’t be guaranteed regular first-team minutes after coming through the academy.

  • The Ecuador international has found himself in and out of the Blues starting lineup this season due to several fitness issues.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By Darren Plant | 26 Nov 2026 15:41.

Chelsea manager Xabi Alonso has revealed that Moises Caicedo is available for Friday's Premier League fixture against Nottingham Forest.

The Ecuador international has found himself in and out of the Blues starting lineup this season due to several fitness issues.

Caicedo's latest injury came during the first half of last weekend's game versus Leeds United, the midfielder landing awkwardly on his back and needing to be withdrawn.

As a result, Caicedo has been an obvious injury doubt for what is a potentially-crucial game for Alonso after three defeats in four top-flight games.

However, speaking at his pre-match press conference, the Spaniard declared Caicedo available for selection.

He told reporters: "Yes, he's going to be OK for tomorrow.".

On a negative note, Alonso acknowledged that Joao Pedro would remain sidelined for the trip to the East Midlands.

Meanwhile, providing an patch on Maxence Lacroix's hamstring injury, he added: "It's one less week than the last game so we are closer to recovery but not for this game.".

There have been reports which suggest that Lacroix could return earlier than the initial target return period of January.

With Lacroix still injured, Alonso may feel forced to start Wesley Fofana alongside Levi Colwill, despite being furious with the Frenchman's comments in an interview this week.

There is the possibility of Josh Acheampong starting in the centre with Colwill, with Marco Palestra potentially starting at right-back.

If Jorrel Hato remains sidelined with a back injury, Pep Chavarria is favourite to start at left-back.

Alonso also has the option of going with a back three featuring the aforementioned centre-backs, with Pedro Neto at right wing-back and Palestra on the left.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Published: 05:00 EST, 22 November 2026 | Updated: 15:14 EST, 25 November 2026.

In a sport obsessed with the next big thing, there is more attention than ever being paid to teenage prodigies who appear destined for the very top.

Recent findings suggest that the latest player to have fans raving is former Manchester United academy star JJ Gabriel, 16, who joined the club aged nine but stunned those at Old Trafford by asking to leave. He is now closing in on a move to Real Madrid.

The acrimonious nature of the teenager's departure has left Gabriel vulnerable to a spectacular fall from grace, particularly after his team released montages showing him joining an agency and saying goodbye to United.

The spotlight is well and truly burning on Gabriel, and he would do well to learn the lessons of other youngsters who were tipped for greatness but ultimately crashed and burned.

Of course, injuries, personal issues and media pressure can all weigh heavily on a young player's prospects. There are countless pitfalls that mean tomorrow's stars often burn out before they have had the chance to shine.

Here, Daily Mail Sport runs the rule over some of the most famous wonderkids who never managed to live up to their potential.

Wonderkid JJ Gabriel, 16, confirmed his exit from Manchester United on Tuesday night.

In a recent development, in 2004, Freddy Adu was viewed as the future of American football. Dubbed 'The Next Pele', the Ghanaian-born talent was the youngest professional athlete in major American sports when he signed his first contract at just 14.

Industry observers note that the hype was extraordinary. He became MLS's highest-paid player, secured a lucrative Nike contract and appeared in an advert alongside Pele himself.

It has been revealed that but things never quite worked out for the attacking midfielder. After three years at DC United and Real Salt Lake, he made the much-anticipated move to Europe, joining Benfica for £1million in 2007. It was largely downhill from there.

After making just 11 appearances in three years in Portugal, he moved to Monaco before embarking on a series of unsuccessful and increasingly disappointing loan spells in Portugal, Turkey and Greece. He eventually ended up at Brazilian club Bahia in 2013.

Recent findings suggest that from that point, Adu floated around clubs in Brazil, Serbia, Finland, the US and Sweden. He last played competitive fooball for Swedish third-tier side Osterlen in 2021, aged 32. He remains one of football's biggest 'what if' stories.

Freddy Adu was dubbed 'The Next Pele' but he never fulfilled anywhere near his potential.

Once described by Sir Alex Ferguson as 'the best player I have ever seen at his age', Ravel Morrison is a particularly unfortunate case of an English prospect failing to make the most of an extraordinarily promising career.

As a fresh-faced 17-year-old, he arrived at Carrington with the talent and ability to become one of the world's best players.

According to recent reports, he had all the attributes of a world-class attacking midfielder and appeared mature beyond his years on the pitch. Off it, however, was a different story.

In early 2011, barely a year after signing his first professional contract with Manchester United, he was charged with witness intimidation in connection with a domestic violence case.

Since then, although he has never served time in prison, Morrison has faced several further charges, including assault, harassment and fraud. His repeated off-field troubles ultimately derailed a career that had once promised so much.

Morrison has gone on to represent 15 clubs during a career spanning 16 years, failing to fulfil the promise that once enchanted Ferguson. He is right now plying his trade in the second tier of UAE football.

Ravel Morrison was one of the most talented players to come through Man United's academy.

It has been revealed that the first Brazilian on this list is former Manchester City forward Robinho. Having come through the Santos academy – a production line that has also delivered the likes of Pele and Neymar – he was expected to become the next superstar to emerge from the club's illustrious ranks.

It has been revealed that however, a series of setbacks meant he never quite fulfilled that early promise. Robinho followed in the footsteps of Brazilian stars such as Adriano, Dani Alves and Kaka by moving to Europe at a young age, joining Real Madrid in 2005.

He enjoyed a promising start to his career, making more than 100 appearances for Los Blancos and winning two league titles before turning 24.

Industry observers note that but his move to Manchester City in 2008 failed to take his career to the next level. In fact, things began to unravel.

The Brazilian did not get off to the best of starts. Upon arriving in Manchester, he revealed that 'Chelsea had made a great proposal, and I accepted'.

What followed were two underwhelming years at the Etihad, where he scored 16 goals in 53 appearances and spent much of his second season in England sidelined by injury.

Sources indicate that robinho subsequently joined AC Milan before spells with a number of Turkish clubs and a return to Brazil. He never again reached the heights of his early career.

Sources indicate that the Brazilian is at the moment imprisoned after being found guilty of sexual assault in connection with an incident at a Milan nightclub in 2013. He began serving his nine-year sentence in 2024.

Former Man City star Robinho never quite fulfilled the early promise he had back in Brazil.

Another case reminiscent of Adu's: a young superstar who was seemingly rated too highly before we ever really got to see him play.

Mastour caught the eye of Italian giants AC Milan after gaining notoriety on YouTube. His video, uploaded in 2012 and titled 'The Best 14-year-old in the World', showcased the Moroccan's impressive array of skills and tricks, making him one of football's first viral sensations.

The hype surrounding Mastour was staggering, with the youngster securing a lucrative endorsement deal with Nike. Before long, he was posing alongside Neymar in a photoshoot.

It has been revealed that but the success never materialised for the tricky forward. During four years on AC Milan's books, he failed to make a single first-team appearance and managed just six outings during loan spells at Malaga and Dutch side PEC Zwolle.

The Moroccan, now 28, plays in the fourth tier of Italian football. Quite how such a highly rated prospect failed to fulfil his potential remains a mystery.

Hachim Mastour dazzled as a teenager on the internet but ended up a long way from the top.

From one player who never demonstrated his quality to one who only a decade ago was the recipient of the coveted Golden Boy award for the best under-21 player in Europe.

Renato Sanches was an absolute phenomenon, the box-to-box midfielder burst onto the scene in the 2015-16 season at Benfica – earning himself a place on the plane to France with Portugal for the 2016 Euros where he played a pivotal role in his nation's triumph.

Those performances saw a host of European giants fight it out to land the then-18-year-old, with Bayern Munich emerging triumphant – landing the midfielder in a deal rising to £63million.

However, Sanches failed to hit his stride in Germany and he was soon shipped out on loan to Swansea – where he was best remembered for passing the ball to an advertising hoarding.

Industry observers note that he enjoyed a small resurgence at Lille, winning Ligue 1 and the French Super Cup, paving the way for a move to PSG. But once again, the big transfer failed to work out, and he now finds himself with Greek side Panathinaikos.

He enjoyed a resurgence at Lille, winning Ligue 1 and the French Super Cup, which paved the way for a move to Paris Saint-Germain.

But once again, a significant-money move failed to work out, and he now finds himself at Greek side Panathinaikos.

Renato Sanches (pictured at Roma in 2024) now plies his trade in Greece with Panathinaikos.

Alexandre Pato had the world at his feet, but his body ultimately failed to deliver on the extraordinary talent he possessed.

It has been revealed that the Brazilian was an electric centre-forward who lit up European football. His goal against Barcelona in the Champions League, scored after just 24 seconds at the age of 22, was a perfect illustration of his frightening ability.

His pace, agility and clinical finishing saw him touted as a future world-beater, while he was named Golden Boy.

Alexandre Pato is another wonderkid who saw their career hampered by a string of injuries.

Yet persistent injury problems made it almost impossible for Pato to fulfil his early promise.

The Brazilian struggled with ankle, Achilles and muscle problems throughout his career. As the injuries mounted, his outstanding physical attributes began to wane, rendering the qualities that had once terrified defenders increasingly ineffective.

Sources indicate that after six years at AC Milan, Pato returned to Brazil to join Corinthians. He spent two years with the club before embarking on short spells at Chelsea and Villarreal, neither of which yielded lasting success.

Rounding off this list is another English talent who once looked destined for the very top but has since seen his career take a downward turn.

It has been revealed that back in 2019, there were few hotter prospects in world football than Jadon Sancho. The then 19-year-old had made the brave decision two years earlier to leave England, having spent several impressive years in Manchester City's academy, and join Bundesliga giants Borussia Dortmund.

It seemed a bizarre move at the time, but the switch proved to be a stroke of genius. Sancho was handed regular first-team football and flourished, registering 40 goals and 54 assists in just 118 Bundesliga appearances. He also collected a DFB-Pokal winner's medal.

By 2021, the boy from Kennington had the world at his feet, with a host of suitors willing to break the bank to secure his services.

Jadon Sancho once had the world at his feet but has found himself stuck in a downward spiral.

Recent findings suggest that after a summer-long transfer saga, Sancho eventually joined Manchester United for an eye-watering £73million, reportedly earning £350,000 per week. It proved to be a nightmare move for both parties.

The Englishman had to wait until late November to score his first United goal in his debut season and never consistently rediscovered his best form.

In January 2024, he returned to Germany and enjoyed a revival, helping guide Dortmund to the Champions League final, where they lost to Real Madrid at Wembley.

Two unsuccessful loan spells at Chelsea and Aston Villa followed before Sancho left United as a free agent last summer. He remains without a club at the age of 26, just five years after his mega-money move.

For all the promising youngsters who struggle to live up to the hype, there are also teen sensations who navigate the pitfalls of professional football to achieve great things.

Kylian Mbappe helped Monaco win their first Ligue 1 title for 17 years having broken into the team as a 16-year-old. His progress since then has been remarkable and he remains one of the world's very best at Real Madrid.

His team-mate Vinicius Jr signed for Real Madrid to much fanfare as an 18-year-old and has lived up to it all for both club and country.

While you could argue that Neymar could have achieved more, he has still enjoyed a stellar career across the globe and become the highest-scoring Brazilian player in history for the national side after signing for Barcelona, as one of the most talked-about starlets.

Wayne Rooney broke through for Everton at 16 and went on to have a brilliant career.

When you look closer to home, Wayne Rooney and Michael Owen broke through as exciting 16-year-olds and both reached the very highest level.

Paolo Maldini made his AC Milan debut at 16 and became one of the all-time great centre-backs and Cesc Fabregas developed into a world class midfielder after getting selected at the same age for Arsenal.

Going back further, Diego Maradona was playing senior football at 15, as did Ronaldo Nazario, while Lionel Messi embarked on his extraordinary career at 16.

JJ Gabriel and his management will be hoping that when all is said and done - his name is associated with this category and avoid joining the starlets who never quite made it.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Manchester United fans have it out at referee Szymon Marciniak and UEFA over a host of controversial decisions during their 2-2 draw with Sporting in the Champions League.

The 2022 World Cup final ref pointed to the spot for a soft Sporting penalty in the first half, though Luis Suarez’s spot kick was saved by Senne Lammens. Minutes later Lammens went from hero to zero when rushing out of his goal and taking out Maximiliano Araujo for another penalty. Suarez made amends from 12 yards.

Amad Diallo thought he had equalised, only for his goal to be ruled out for a foul by Youri Tielemans in the build-up, which earned the midfielder a yellow card after some vigorous protests.

Man Utd received a penalty of their own early in the second half also bordered on soft; Lisandro Martinez going down very easily after Eduardo Quaresma’s clumsy challenge.

Bruno Fernandes converted and then two minutes later benefitted from a divot of his own creation, albeit inadvertently, to hand Man Utd the lead, when he low, driven shot flicked up off the pitch to beat keeper Kaique Pereira.

A chaos continued when a Lammens howler saw Sporting equaliser, the keeper failing to deal with a cross to allow Suarez to instinctively, and acrobatically, finish from close range.

And then, at the other end of the pitch, an extremely similar scenario occurred as Pereira palmed the ball into his own net at a Man Utd corner for what appeared to be the winner.

In a recent development, referee Marciniak initially awarded the goal, but VAR ordered a pitchside review which saw Martinez and Patrick Dorgu penalised for a foul on the keeper. There was still time for a red card as Tielemans was shown a second yellow for a late, studs up challenge.

The performance stirred up plenty of frustrations among the fanbase, especially in light of Leny Yoro’s red card against Liverpool which was later overturned by the Premier League.

There were plenty of fans, both with an affiliation to Man utd and not, claiming a “robbery”.

A Man Utd fan remarked one of the decisions “boiled his blood”, while others were left waiting for another apology after the Yoro debacle.

But one Man City fan saw things slightly differently, insisting very decision was “spot on”...

Omar Marmoush has backed his "unbelievable" Tottenham team-mate Luca Williams-Barnett to have a "very massive future".

The teenager has impressed under Roberto De Zerbi in recent weeks, most notably scoring and assisting in their Premier League win over Ipswich Town last weekend.

Aged 18 years and 51 days, Williams-Barnett became the second-youngest player to score and assist in a Premier League game, behind Michael Owen.

He also became the fourth-youngest player to score on his first Premier League start, behind Daniel Jebbison in May 2021 (17y 276d), Danny Cadamarteri in September 1997 (17y 343d) and Mark Cullen in May 2010 (18y 12d).

Should he start and score against Sunderland on Sunday, he'd be the youngest player to score in his first two starts (18 years, 59 days).

The forward's breakthrough into the Spurs' first team was rewarded with a new contract, which is reported to be a five-year deal, and Marmoush believes the only way is up for the exciting winger.

"He is unbelievable," Marmoush told Sky sports about Williams-Barnett.

Sources indicate that it's always been Tottenham. https://t.co/W3mx3ZQIH9.

— Tottenham Hotspur (@SpursOfficial) November 24, 2026.

"He is a great, great talent and what I like most about him, of course, his talent is something that everyone sees, is that he is very brave, too.

According to recent reports, "And when he came on in his first game, he just took the ball and tried things. He is very direct, tries to beat his opponent and he has a very, very promising future ahead of him.

Recent findings suggest that "He has got it, and you can see that. One of the substantial traits of a big talent, and a big player, is the personality and the character and that is what stands out most for me, his courage and to be brave.

"As a young lad, to come into Spurs' first team and perform like that is not easy, and just to believe in yourself and do the actions on your pitch is great.

"I hope he is enjoying it, and he will have a very, very big future, that's for sure.".

Are you going back to being the player we saw in Brugge?

“I also like being the kind of player who can help the team with my personality on the pitch.

Liverpool’s £400m front line clicks but win at Brentford turns on red card

📅 17 Oct 2026 | ⏱️ 25 min read (5005 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Co

⏱️ ~25 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Only time will tell if Liverpool’s £400m front line can ever justify the extraordinary amount of money that was spent on them, but this was at least a significant step in the right direction.
  • Industry observers note that admittedly, the task was made significantly easier by the major turning point of this game: a red card for Brentford’s Yehor Yarmoliuk.
  • But as the context of the match changed, so did the level of threat from the visitors.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Only time will tell if Liverpool’s £400m front line can ever justify the extraordinary amount of money that was spent on them, but this was at least a significant step in the right direction. In a gritty victory away to Brentford, all four of Alexander Isak, Florian Wirtz, Bradley Barcola and Victor Muñoz either scored or assisted goals.

Industry observers note that admittedly, the task was made significantly easier by the major turning point of this game: a red card for Brentford’s Yehor Yarmoliuk. At the time of Yarmoliuk’s “headbutting action” towards Liverpool defender Jeremy Jacquet, the visitors were trailing 1-0 and looking worryingly short of ideas in attack.

But as the context of the match changed, so did the level of threat from the visitors. Against 10 men, with more space in which to operate, Liverpool’s forwards looked increasingly dangerous. Wirtz began to pull the strings, Barcola started to cause problems, Muñoz stretched the Brentford defence and Isak became a lurking menace.

According to recent reports, for Andoni Iraola, who had failed to beat Brentford in six attempts as manager of Bournemouth, it would have made for an immensely pleasing sight. After last weekend’s thrashing by Manchester City, Liverpool have responded with a 6-3 Champions League win over LASK and this victory against a previously unbeaten Brentford. Iraola will know, however, that his team’s numerical advantage was the fundamental reason for the dramatic shift in the flow of this game.

In a recent development, the Gtech Community Stadium simmered with outrage following Yarmoliuk’s red card, which came in the eighth minute of first-half stoppage time, and the home fans probably had a point. Yes, there was a movement of the midfielder’s head towards Jacquet, but it was hardly an act of violence. Jacquet’s reaction, collapsing to the turf in mock agony, was embarrassing but predictably effective. Cynics would say the Frenchman changed the game for his team. Purists would argue this is no way in which to influence a match.

Keith Andrews, the Brentford head coach, chose against complaining too aggressively. But he did make it clear what he thought of Jacquet’s behaviour. “I do think they were cute and clever,” Andrews said. “He is walking into Yarmo. But we need to look at ourselves and I understand why it was a red. Yarmo is an amazing young man and he will learn from this.”.

It has been revealed that brentford had been the better team before this decisive incident and they deserved their lead, given to them by a majestic header by Keane Lewis-Potter, from Igor Thiago’s cross. It was a moment of attacking quality that Iraola’s glitzy attackers had looked unlikely to replicate, especially when Barcola fluffed a one-versus-one showdown with Brentford goalkeeper Caoimhin Kelleher.

To play an entire half of Premier League football with only 10 men is a brutal examination, though, and Brentford were unable to pass the test. Wirtz unleashed Muñoz after an hour, allowing the Spaniard to fire home with his left foot, before Barcola’s header found Isak in the box with 20 minutes remaining.

It was Isak’s fifth goal of the campaign, which means he has now beaten last season’s tally of four. He has scored in all five of his Premier League appearances against Brentford. “I didn’t have too many chances,” Isak mentioned. “I was waiting for my moment.”.

Any hopes of a Brentford comeback evaporated in stoppage time, when the home side lost another man to a red card. This time it was Vitaly Janelt, who received his second yellow for fouling Rio Ngumoha, Liverpool’s sparkling teenage winger. From there, Liverpool’s attempts to score a third were comically poor. “We lacked some composure,” admitted Iraola. “But it was a good battle today, and very important points for us. To take three points here is very valuable.”.

In a recent development, an encouraging result for Liverpool, then, but this was not an afternoon without concerns. The first-half showing was worrying, and there were also injuries to Dominik Szoboszlai and Jeremie Frimpong. Both players limped off, and Iraola said they will now be out “for some time”.

The loss of Szoboszlai will be a particular concern, as he was rushed back from a hamstring injury for this game but then felt the same muscle again after only 32 minutes of action. “It’s a very delicate situation,” said Iraola.

Industry observers note that the injury to Frimpong meant that Muñoz, a winger, played most of the second half as an attack-minded right-back. He did so excellently, and took his goal with impressive composure after Wirtz had pushed the ball into his path. Liverpool’s second was similarly clinical, as Isak pounced on Barcola’s knock-down in a congested penalty area. These, clearly, are the moments of game-changing quality that Liverpool expect from their significant-money forwards. Iraola will hope it was a sign of things to come.

Industry observers note that speaking to Sky Sports after his first Premier League win as Fulham head coach, Arbeloa noted: “I’m so happy, happy for my players, happy for my supporters, happy for everyone at the club that they deserve this victory. We [waited] a lot of time and some many games that I think we deserved this victory before, but today we did a very good game and yes, I can’t believe that the game finished just 1-0.”.

By Ellis Stevens | 26 Nov 2026 15:41.

Two teams at the bottom of the Scottish Premiership standings will do battle on Saturday, when St Mirren welcome Kilmarnock to the Marbill Coaches Stadium.

The hosts are 10th in the table with 14 points from 14 games, while the visitors are propping up the standings with just nine points from 14 fixtures.

St Mirren initially enjoyed a positive start to the 2026-27 Scottish Premiership season, winning three and drawing one of their opening four league fixtures.

However, Craig McLeish's side subsequently endured a miserable run of results, going on to record just one win in their next 10 league fixtures.

The Saints have suffered eight defeats during that run, alongside one draw, leading to St Mirren rapidly falling to 10th in the Scottish Premiership table with just 14 points.

St Mirren, now just one point above the drop zone, face a particularly notable match in the early relegation battle, as a win against Kilmarnock would extend their lead over the bottom-placed side to a healthy eight points.

On the other hand, a defeat, which would mark their fourth consecutive loss, would see St Mirren's current five-point lead slashed to just two points.

Despite their ongoing struggles, the Saints have been at their best at home, including winning one, drawing one and losing one of their last three home fixtures.

Kilmarnock, meanwhile, are enduring a dismal 2026-27 league campaign, sitting at the bottom of the standings with just nine points after 14 matchdays.

Neil McCann's side have recorded two wins, three draws and suffered nine defeats in their 14 league games, including remaining winless in their last five matches, with four losses and one draw.

Kilmarnock's biggest weakness has undeniably been their defensive vulnerability, having conceded 33 goals in 14 league matches - seven more than any other team in the division.

However, Killie are equally ineffective in offence, having scored just 15 goals in 14 games - only St Mirren (13) have scored fewer in the league.

Despite their disappointing campaign to date, Kilmarnock do boast a strong recent record against St Mirren, winning three of the last five encounters, although they did lose 1-0 earlier this term.

Kilmarnock Scottish Premiership form:.

St Mirren will be without Nikolas Agrafiotis, Jonah Ayunga, Malik Dijksteel and Keanu Baccus for this match due to injury problems.

Killian Phillips is St Mirren's top scorer (four) and joint-top assister (two) in the league this season, and the attacking midfielder should start behind Eseosa Sule in attack.

Meanwhile, Max Stryjek remains unavailable due to a knee injury, leaving Nico Mantl to continue in goal.

George Stanger and Michael John Kamara should provide protection in central defence, with Tom Lowery, Aaron Tshibola and Greg Kiltie featuring in midfield.

St Mirren possible starting lineup:.

Chapman; Ramsay, Gogic, Jackson, John; Carr, Nsio; Thomas, Phillips, Kabia; Sule.

Kilmarnock possible starting lineup:.

Mantl; McCarthy, Kamara, Stanger, Schjonning-Larsen; Tshibola, Lowery; Ring, Kiltie, Owen; Hugill.

Ex-Manchester United star Ashley Young labelled the performance of referee Szymon Marciniak during Wednesday’s chaotic Champions League draw with Sporting as a “disgrace”.

Marciniak was at the centre of multiple controversial decisions in a dramatic 2-2 league phase tie in Lisbon, awarding three penalties, ruling out two Man Utd goals and sending off midfielder Youri Tielemans in stoppage time.

New Red Devils boss Mauricio Pochettino claimed that his side had been “punished” by the officials, going on to say that it was “impossible” to understand how the decisions were reached.

Young held a similar position, with the former winger left searching for words when speaking about Marciniak’s display.

The ex-United captain noted on BBC Radio 5 Live: “The referee’s performance was just simply… wow.

“The decisions that he gave… Youri Tielemans getting booked, to eventually getting sent off later because you booked him when it should never have been a booking, and it should have been an equalising goal.

“The third goal that should have stood because he’s saying Patrick Dorgu fouled the ‘keeper.

In a recent development, “The ‘keeper comes out and flaps at it before he is even touched. How that has gone to VAR is beyond me. His decision-making today is nothing more than a disgrace.”.

Sources indicate that united fans would have been further irked by the decision to rule out their potential late winner, as Sporting’s equaliser came in a similar fashion. Goalkeeper Senne Lammens dropped a high ball under light pressure, allowing Luis Suarez to convert with an improvised bicycle kick.

However, talkSPORT pundit Gabby Agbonlahor believes the reaction to the refereeing controversies has been overblown.

He said on Thursday morning: “Manchester United fans, just get on with it. You didn’t deserve to win the game.

According to recent reports, “Did the referee make a couple of mistakes? Yes, he did. But come on. Manchester United fans - first they’re moaning about the owners, next they’re moaning about chief executives, [Omar] Berrada, [Jason] Wilcox. Now it’s referees every game, it’s VAR every game.

“How about - you didn’t deserve to win the game? The referee didn’t make Lisandro Martinez make a stupid challenge to give away the first penalty that gets saved.

“The referee didn’t make [Noussair] Mazraoui come in so tight to the centre-half and allow the [Sporting] left-back flying forward.

In a recent development, “The referee didn’t make Lammens come out to no man’s land. I don’t know what he’s doing. I don’t know what he’s going to achieve running out there.

“The referee didn’t make Lammens have chocolate wrists and drop the ball when no one is on him.”.

The draw with Sporting leaves United 19th in the Champions League table, with three games remaining in this season’s league phase.

Tielemans’ red card means the Belgian will miss their next European fixture - a home tie with Bundesliga outfit RB Leipzig on December 8.

Tonali missed Spurs’ 2-0 victory at home to Ipswich last Saturday due to illness, as Roberto De Zerbi’s side earned three points on their return from the international break, but is set to be available for selection when Spurs travel to the Stadium of Light on Sunday.

Savio, meanwhile, was named on the bench against Ipswich, having missed the last four games with a muscular injury. The 22-year-old was introduced in the second half, but lasted just 26 minutes before he had to come off injured.

Savio was visibly upset as he headed down the tunnel, and De Zerbi confirmed he had suffered a recurrence of the same injury that had kept him out for the last six weeks.

"I'm sorry for Savio's injury, because it was the same injury as last time, and we need him. He's a crucial player for us,” De Zerbi noted in his post-match press conference.

“He’s unlucky in this period. We have to be close with him to help him to become the top player we bought at the beginning of this season.".

Savio is expected to join fellow wingers Mathys Tel and Mykhailo Mudryk on the sidelines, meaning teenage sensation Luca Williams-Barnett, who scored and assisted on his full senior debut against Ipswich, could be in line for more minutes.

Fears over an injury to Omar Marmoush have been allayed after the forward was spotted in training footage.

Centre-back Tosin Adarabioyo is expected to be available for selection again after returning from a calf injury. Tosin was fit to play against Ipswich, but De Zerbi chose not to take any unnecessary risks.

Syndicated reporting provided by Stats Perform and reviewed by the SoccerNews editorial team.

Dominic Calvert-Lewin said the love he has received from the Leeds United fans is the main reason behind signing a new contract at Elland Road.

It was declared on Thursday that Calvert-Lewin, who joined Leeds on a free transfer last summer, has put pen to paper on a fresh deal that will keep him at the club until 2029.

The news comes after the 29-year-old was linked with a move to Manchester United, but Calvert-Lewin has instead committed his future to Daniel Farke's side.

Since the start of last season, Calvert-Lewin has scored more Premier League goals than any other English player (19), which earned him a recall to the England squad.

His 19 goals in 46 top-flight games for Leeds in this time are two more than he scored in 92 games across his final four campaigns with Everton (17).

On his relationship with the Leeds supporters, Calvert-Lewin told the club's website: "I've felt the love – I'm not just saying it, I really have – and that's why I wanted to stay.

According to recent reports, "I do think my goals have helped our connection. I also think the fans identify with the way I play. What they expect from their number nine is naturally what I do in my game.

"I'm physical, I run a lot, I try to make life difficult for defenders, I put quality in there and I score goals.

"Our relationship has just grown and grown, so hopefully it continues growing now.".

The journey continues! https://t.co/SmY0uWKAKF.

— Leeds United (@LUFC) November 26, 2026.

Calvert-Lewin has scored six goals and provided one assist in 13 appearances in all competitions this season for Leeds, who sit seventh in the Premier League.

He follows in the footsteps of Ethan Ampadu, Joe Rodon, Jayden Bogle and Brenden Aaronson in agreeing to fresh terms, with two more players reportedly set to join them.

It is believed that Ao Tanaka is set to sign a deal keeping him at the club until 2029, while Leeds are said to be willing to trigger Lukas Nmecha's one-year extension.

Following victories over Spurs and Chelsea, Leeds are looking to win three consecutive Premier League games for the first time since May 2021 (a run of four) when they welcome Coventry City to Elland Road on Saturday.

Manchester City have been given an update on their appeal against the Premier League's financial charges ahead of this weekend’s huge title clash with Arsenal.

Sources indicate that city were in October found guilty of 114 breaches of the league's financial rules, with an independent commission concluding the club had used "sham" commercial contracts to disguise more than £830million in funding between 2009 and 2018. The commission also found the Man City had made "concerted efforts to stop and frustrate" the investigation.

The club have consistently denied wrongdoing, and an appeal was immediately introduced with a result expected in early 2027.

Speculation over possible punishments, should the appeal prove unsuccessful, range from a fine to various points deductions and even expulsion from the Premier League, all the while Man City‘s form on the pitch has suffered a dip.

In a recent development, city have won just one of their last five games across all competitions, and have lost three of their last four in the Premier League to see their title hopes handed a huge blow. Arsenal is up next on Sunday in a game Erling Haaland has already described as their “toughest of the season”.

Amid the on-pitch struggles, financial expert Stefan Borson, who previously worked as a financial advisor to City, expects there to be clarity sooner rather than later over the club’s off-pitch concerns.

"We're told that it will be mid-December,” Borson noted, regarding the appeal hearing, on Football Uncensored with Piers Morgan and Simon Jordan.

“Because of the way the days fall, that's likely to start on the 12th.

"It's likely to go for between five and 10 days, it seems, and therefore finish before Christmas. And then we wait for a decision. Ordinarily, that decision would take quite some time.

"I suspect that certainly the Premier League want to get it expedited so they get a decision and can then have the sanction hearing and the sanction appeal, which is inevitable either way, in before the end of the season so they can effectively sanction City and punish them this season.".

Borson suggested a timetable may already have been agreed, with the Premier League keen to avoid further legal complications.

Recent findings suggest that "In the rulebook that came out at the start of the season, the rules changed and you had an expedited timetable. In any event, a case like City's and an appeal like City's would never fall within the standardised timetable.

"I think most likely the parties have ultimately agreed some form of timetable which means that any argument from City in the future about the process goes away.

It has been revealed that "The last thing the Premier League will want is to give City another reason to take legal action under Rule X or otherwise and to say, actually the whole appeal process, not only was the old process flawed but we didn't even have a fair appeal. Because if they do that, we're back to square one.".

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By Jonathan O'Shea | 26 Nov 2026 15:49, Last updated: 26 Nov 2026 15:54.

Now down to third in the Serie A standings, Scudetto holders Inter Milan will try to give their title defence a boost when Genoa visit San Siro on Saturday night.

Recent results have seen Inter slip behind both Rome clubs, but they gained a vital European victory in midweek; meanwhile, their visitors have surged into the top half after recovering from a rocky start.

Having exited at the first knockout round last season, Inter started this term's Champions League campaign by taking nothing from their first two fixtures - but​ things have improved dramatically since then.

Three straight wins without conceding have moved them up the table, and Cristian Chivu's side now occupy a playoff place - in fact, finishing inside the top eight cannot be ruled out.

After defeating Shakhtar Donetsk and Feyenoord, the Nerazzurri beat Stuttgart 2-0 on Wednesday night, as captain Lautaro Martinez scored his first goal since returning from injury.

That partly made amends for throwing away two Serie A points three days beforehand, when Inter played out a chaotic 4-4 draw with local rivals Atalanta BC.

Despite Pio Esposito's first top-flight hat-trick, they let in a couple of avoidable late goals that left them three points behind surprise leaders Lazio, with Roma sandwiched between.

Now, the Nerazzurri will aim to put pressure on both capital clubs by posting a customary home win over Genoa.

Such has been their dominance, Inter have won all of the last 12 league meetings at San Siro, keeping 10 clean sheets and only conceding two goals.

Either home or away, Genoa have won none of their last 14 clashes with Inter, so they may be dreading an upcoming double-header.

Just days after this league game, the Grifone must return to Milan for a cup tie, as the sides vie for a place in the Coppa Italia quarter-finals.

Though their past record makes for grim reading, present form suggests Genoa can at least give the Italian champions a scare, as they have won five of their last seven Serie A matches.

Since Daniele De Rossi swerved the sack during the October international break, his rejuvenated side have shot up the table, swapping the drop zone for the top half.

Last weekend, the Rossoblu beat lowly Sassuolo 2-0 thanks to a Milutin Osmajic brace, posting back-to-back away wins for the first time since 2024.

Some 12 years have passed since Genoa recorded three successive away wins at Italy's elite level, and few would expect them to do so on Saturday.

Inter Milan form (all competitions):.

Inter will be missing set-piece specialist Hakan Calhanoglu and back-up striker Ange Bonny due to thigh injuries, while Piotr Zielinski and Alessandro Bastoni are both doubts.

Bastoni was substituted before half time against Stuttgart, and it remains to be seen if he will recover from a muscular problem in time to play.

After scoring as a substitute in midweek, Martinez must vie with Marcus Thuram and in-form Esposito to feature up front.

According to recent reports, level with the latter pair in the Capocannoniere race, Genoa striker Osmajic has scored six goals in his first 12 Serie A appearances. The Montenegrin is almost certain to start, as fellow forward Lorenzo Colombo suffered an ACL injury last weekend, probably curtailing his 2026-27 campaign.

Leo Ostigard was recently hospitalised with a high fever, but he is still expected to lead the visitors' three-man defence in Milan.

Key midfielder Morten Frendrup has been struggling with an ankle issue, meaning he faces a race against time.

Inter Milan possible starting lineup:.

Recent findings suggest that J. Martinez; Bisseck, Akanji, Augusto; Spence, Barella, Sucic, Jones, Dimarco; Esposito, L. Martinez.

Genoa possible starting lineup:.

Bijlow; Marcandalli, Ostigard, Vasquez; Ehizibue, Frendrup, Traore, Ellertsson; Messias, El Shaarawy; Osmajic.

Not only are they traditionally dominant in this fixture, but Inter have also won all of their last six Serie A home games while scoring at least twice.

Though they sometimes start slowly - and Genoa have scored a remarkable 77% of their league goals during the first half - the Nerazzurri will not be stopped.

#140742. Industry News: THE BREAKDOWN: The real reasons why Enzo Maresca's Man City can't stop losing - from anonymous Enzo Fernandez abandoning Elliot Anderson, to the fatal flaws in Italian's set-up that are being brutally exposed

Industry News: THE BREAKDOWN: The real reasons why Enzo Maresca's Man City can't stop losing - from anonymous Enzo Fernandez abandoning Elliot Anderson, to the fatal flaws in Italian's set-up that are being brutally exposed

📅 20 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 9 min read (1736 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Dailymail

⏱️ ~9 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Published: 07:00 EST, 20 November 2026 | Updated: 05:23 EST, 26 November 2026.
  • Sources indicate that diet Pep is losing his fizz.
  • Seven successive Premier League wins to start his City reign, a record for a new manager in the competition, breaking one jointly-held by Guardiola, gave the impression that this might be a smooth passing of the torch after all.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Published: 07:00 EST, 20 November 2026 | Updated: 05:23 EST, 26 November 2026.

Sources indicate that diet Pep is losing his fizz. Enzo Maresca may look like Pep Guardiola, may have learned his craft under his Manchester City predecessor, but his quest to follow in his mentor’s footsteps has all gone a bit flat.

Seven successive Premier League wins to start his City reign, a record for a new manager in the competition, breaking one jointly-held by Guardiola, gave the impression that this might be a smooth passing of the torch after all.

Three months in, and three defeats on the spin that left them six points behind Arsenal have made it clear that something is not clicking for Maresca.

Sources indicate that is the uncertainty around the potential punishment following that guilty verdict taking its toll? Is Maresca just suffering from his usual late autumn dips? He suffered similar tricky periods around late October and early November at Leicester and his first season at Chelsea too.

Or is there something at the heart of his side, of his system, that’s finally being exposed?

Enzo Maresca's Man City have slumped to three straight Premier League defeats after a promising start to the season.

Guardiola’s City was all about control. Keep the ball, dominate the pitch, play the game at your pace, on your terms.

Industry observers note that maresca’s City, regardless of how well they started the season, has been about anything but. It has been about triumph amid chaos, about moments of magic more than the overarching method.

It has been revealed that without that control, City’s defensive concerns have been laid bare. The 13 goals they have let in after 10 games is their most at this stage since 2008. They haven’t kept a clean sheet in their last eight matches in all competitions. That's a drought longer than at any point under Guardiola.

Their biggest problem over City's three successive Premier League defeats is just how susceptible they have been to counter attacks.

Only Newcastle have faced more shots this season following ‘fast breaks’ – data giants Opta's term for counter attacks – than City’s 17, and 11 of those have come in the last three games: six against Nottingham Forest, two of which led to goals, three against Brighton and another two against Aston Villa.

Industry observers note that maresca’s side are being more profligate in possession, too. Over the first seven games of the season, they lost the ball 120 times a game on average – one of the best figures in the division. Since then, it’s closer to 140.

City have been wasteful in possession and regularly overrun on the counter, with Elliot Anderson (centre) too often left isolated in midfield.

ANDERSON CAN'T DO IT ALL ON HIS OWN.

It has been revealed that many of these problems have their roots in Maresca's serious problems in midfield. Rodri, the best holding midfielder of his generation, was always going to be hard to replace but Maresca appears to be expecting Elliot Anderson to do it all on his own.

Industry observers note that anderson is at his best when he’s free to get up and down the pitch, box to box, using his physicality not just in winning the ball back but progressing it. No midfielder played more passes into the final third last season than Anderson at Forest. At one stage of the campaign, he had played more progressive passes than any other player across Europe’s top five leagues.

And yet Maresca is forcing Anderson to play as the sitter while his golden boy Enzo Fernandez, whom he pushed City to sign in the summer for £125million, is roaming free and high up the pitch.

Maresca likes his teams to build up in a 3-1-6 shape, which sees Fernandez push up as an extra attacking midfielder, and leaves Anderson manning the fort alone.

When City lose the ball, though, it leaves them wide open.

It has been revealed that this is the opening goal City conceded against Forest. Josko Gvardiol wants to play the ball inside but has only red shirts and empty green space ahead of him. Anderson is the only man free, but even he is too high and has a Forest player ready to cut off the pass. Eventually, Gvardiol gets robbed and Forest score.

According to recent reports, A lack of options for Josko Gvardiol (left) led to Forest's opener against City. Enzo Fernandez (circled) was caught high up the pitch, way ahead of the deeper Anderson (also circled).

Here’s another moment in the defeat by Brighton.

The Seagulls break forward on the flank and Anderson races over to close the ball down. Fernandez is, you guessed it, high up the pitch.

City have no midfield cover to stop the ball inside, Abdukodir Khusanov gets drawn in and leaves loads of space in behind for Yasin Ayari to exploit and cross to Maxim De Cuyper for a great chance.

The lack of protection offered by Anderson and especially the more advanced Fernandez was again on show against Brighton, who were able to exploit the acres of space left in midfield.

Fernandez is doing what Maresca wants, but it’s not working. Maresca needs more from him, especially when Anderson’s instincts are to press and harass and bully, which can leave gaps when he does not yet read the game as comprehensively as Rodri.

Anderson sits in the top five for ball recoveries among midfielders to have played 500 minutes this season. Fernandez is in the bottom five. That figure becomes even more alarming when you consider Anderson has created more chances from open play than Fernandez, too.

Sources indicate that ayyoub Bouaddi indicated at the World Cup that he had the most similar profile to Rodri. It might be time for Maresca to put some faith in him.

Recent findings suggest that maresca has always wanted his goalkeeper to be an 11th outfielder. In his one season at Leicester, Mads Hermansen played more passes than any goalkeeper in Championship history. During his time at Chelsea, there was a shaky moment in a draw with Arsenal when loud groans greeted a misplaced pass from Robert Sanchez.

‘I am the guy who asks Robert to do that,’ noted Maresca after that game. ‘The moment he stops doing that, he is not going to play.’.

Donnarumma, though, for all his (usually) excellent shot-stopping, is anything but a ball-playing goalkeeper. The ball rolled under his foot from a simple back pass against Coventry and so nearly crept over the line. He gifted France an early lead while on international duty with Italy when he passed the ball straight to Michael Olise.

Only two keepers made more errors leading to shots than Donnarumma across the course of last season, with many of those being with his feet, like when he gifted Kai Havertz an equaliser in City's victory over Arsenal in April.

Gianluigi Donnarumma has never been good with his feet - now his excellent shot-stopping has taken a dip too.

The Italian should have easily dealt with Nicolas Jackson's second goal in City's 2-1 loss at Aston Villa.

The decision to let James Trafford leave in the summer, especially with Guardiola’s impending departure and a manager like Maresca coming in, is looking ever more misguided.

Trafford is not immune to mistakes either, of course. He erred badly when trying to play out from the back for City against Spurs last season and made an almost identical howler for Leeds at Bournemouth in October. But he is still far more confident at playing out from the back than Donnarumma.

The double blow for Maresca is that the trade-off with Donnarumma – where he makes up for his weakness with the ball at his feet by making saves that other keepers can’t make – is no longer paying off either.

Nicolas Jackson’s shot squirmed straight through him to hand Villa victory and condemn City to their first defeat of the season.

When you are coughing up chances as frequently as City are, Maresca needs his keeper to be on top form.

Sources indicate that do you know who is keeping the ball out of his net? James Trafford. He boasts the highest save percentage of any goalkeeper in the top flight, keeping out 81 per cent of the shots on target coming his way. Donnarumma is 15th, on less than 66 per cent.

According to Opta’s expected data, Trafford has also prevented more than four goals that he should have conceded from the quality of the shots he’s faced. Again, he’s the best in the Premier League. Donnarumma is middle of the pack.

‘At the moment, I’m not thinking about the goalkeeping situation,’ said Maresca recently. Without Trafford there and just 34-year-old Geronimo Rulli as back-up, he doesn’t really have a choice but to persist with Donnarumma and hope he improves.

When the goals stop flowing for Erling Haaland, City can't mask all their other problems.

So used are we now to seeing the Norwegian on the scoresheet, having notched nine in City’s opening eight matches, that when he goes just two games without a goal it feels as if he’s on a barren spell.

The problem, though, is less down to Haaland and more that City’s build-up in recent weeks is struggling to get him into the game.

City are finding it more difficult to get Haaland on the ball. His touches per game are falling steadily but, crucially, so are the quality of the chances his team-mates are creating for him.

Recent findings suggest that haaland had more than one Opta-defined 'big chance' in five of City’s opening seven games. He’s had just one come his way in each of their three defeats.

In a recent development, his expected goals (xG) tally is dropping too. Across City’s winning streak, Haaland’s average xG per match was 0.81. Only once, against Liverpool, did it drop below 0.5.

Over the three defeats, it’s just 0.45 and has not once gone above 0.5.

Antoine Semenyo missing the last three games through injury has not helped, especially when teams now try to pack the middle of the pitch and force City wide.

Haaland will come good, he always does, but City need to start serving him again if Maresca wants to get through this tricky spell and stop the vultures from circling.

Mikel Arteta’s side are still in fine shape to progress straight through to the last 16 as one of the top-eight sides in the Champions League. Only the Gunners, holders Paris Saint-Germain and Real Madrid remain unbeaten in this season’s competition.

Sources indicate that however, it could have been so much better, after an extraordinarily wasteful display in the draw with Borussia Dortmund on Tuesday night. Arsenal registered 30 shots, but only four on target and they scored just once.

According to recent reports, it should have been so much more for Martin Odegaard, too. He has registered only one assist in Europe this season, ranking him 45th in the competition for that metric.

In a recent development, and yet for expected assists, per FotMob, Odegaard ranks top across the entire Champions League. Above Nico Paz, who has five assists to his name, and Lamine Yamal, who has three.

Arsenal have had no glitch creating chances. Against Dortmund, Odegaard laid on nine of them, the most by any player in a Champions League match this season.

Sources indicate that that was just the second time this decade that an Arsenal player has created more than five chances in a Champions League match. The other example? Odegaard against Napoli in September.

It has been revealed that the discourse around Odegaard is often hypercritical. That, to an extent, is understandable. He has been the captain and creative heartbeat of the team in a period in which, for all it has been successful, there have been ongoing questions surrounding the attack.

It has been revealed that it is perhaps also a hangover from the last two seasons, when injuries hampered Odegaard and he was well off his best. Frustration towards him built and some minds appear to have been made up.

However, the criticism that he does not deliver consistently enough just does not hold up to scrutiny this season.

In a recent development, from the moment Odegaard returned to the club in the summer after a strong World Cup with Norway, he has looked back to his best. That started with his sublime goal against Manchester City in the Community Shield and has continued since.

For all there have been some notable exceptions, Arsenal have on the whole played much better football this season. They have been far more free-flowing and fluid in attack.

It has been revealed that odegaard has been central to that. Along with his chance creation stats in Europe, Odegaard is also second for expected assists in the Premier League.

According to recent reports, he is taking more responsibility in front of goal, too. Odegaard is Arsenal’s top scorer this season and is only one league goal shy of his combined tally from the last two seasons.

Sources indicate that if there has been a dip in Arsenal’s attack from the start of this season, that is not down to Odegaard. Bukayo Saka, who was displaying far better goalscoring instincts, suffering a quad injury, and Kai Havertz’s performance levels dropping significantly are far more relevant explanations.

Arsenal do have a problem in attack - but it is not Odegaard.

Odegaard has been the most consistent forward player. It is not just the chances created or even the goals, but his influence in all facets of Arsenal’s game as almost an extension of Arteta on the pitch. He is the leader of the press, and that led to the winning goal against Liverpool at Anfield earlier this month.

Arsenal do have a problem in attack - but it is not Odegaard. It is not an exaggeration to say that Viktor Gyokeres should have scored another three goals against Dortmund from chances created by Odegaard alone.

It has been revealed that the Gunners are not clinical enough but that is not the fault of the player creating the chances. Nor is it a coaching issue. Arteta could not have done more to deliver a win against Dortmund.

Industry observers note that the problem is a personnel one. The quality of Arsenal’s attackers does not come close to matching the level in every other position in the squad. At least one top-class winger signing is required, along with a new striker.

Industry observers note that it was clear at the end of last season that significant upgrades were needed. Instead, Arsenal sold three forwards and signed only Christos Tzolis.

In a recent development, that is the massive failure and where the fingers should be pointing. Not at Odegaard for occasionally taking too many touches or making a wrong decision on the counter.

Odegaard’s contract situation adds another factor to the debate over his role in the team. He is nearing the final 18 months of his current deal.

Talks have not yet begun over an extension, Odegaard revealed during the international break, but that should be a no-brainer for Arsenal.

That will require the club to make another significant financial commitment, following on from several other latest contracts for key players, but it is still a far cheaper alternative to trying to sign a replacement of Odegaard’s quality.

Securing Odegaard’s future should be the club’s next top priority, swiftly followed by then delivering him the forwards he deserves.

Monza star Gustavo Varela has distanced himself from speculation that he could be set for a January transfer move and insists he is ‘paying no attention’ to incessant rumours linking him with Arsenal, Barcelona and Napoli.

Varela, 21, was deemed surplus to requirements at Benfica and completed a switch to newly promoted Italian outfit Monza for a fee of just €2million (£1.7m) – plus performance-related bonuses – in the summer.

It has proven a tough start to the season for Monza on their return to Serie A, with the club picking up just three wins and languishing down in 14th place in the table.

Varela has proven a shining light up front, though, scoring 11 goals in his opening 11 top-flight appearances, and the striker’s barnstorming form in Lombardy has begun to attract the attentions of European football’s elite.

According to recent reports emanating out of Varela’s native Portugal, Barca, Napoli and Arsenal are all actively pursuing a deal for the forward on the back of his goalscoring exploits in the first three months of the campaign.

Premier League champions Arsenal are said to be among a host of Premier League clubs that have ‘expressed an interest’ in Varela and were ‘one of the first to enquire’ about the player’s potential availability.

It’s understood the Gunners are in the market for an attacker of Varela’s profile, with Viktor Gyokeres struggling to live up to expectations following his £64m arrival from Sporting last year.

On Monday night, Varela ensured he remained in the headlines with a terrific brace in Monza’s 3-0 victory over Fiorentina – in doing so, becoming only the third player in the last 50 years to reach the double figures in their first 11 Serie A games.

‘I can’t believe what I’m doing. I go home, close my eyes and I can’t believe it. Football is made of moments,’ Varela told DAZN Italy following Monza’s win.

On his brilliant flicked effort to complete his double, Varela added: ‘It was pure instinct, it’s not something I practice.

Sources indicate that ‘A very beautiful cross came in, I was close to the goal and I decided to try my luck. If you don’t try, you can’t do it, and it happened.’.
