Varela was then asked for his reaction the rumoured interest he was receiving from some of Europe’s most high-profile teams, to which he responded: ‘I continue to thank Monza for allowing me to be here. It has all been incredible.

‘I feel lucky to be part of this reality and I only hope to continue on this path.

‘I pay no attention to the news. I only focus on what I have to do on the field. It’s normal, it’s part of football.

‘I’m going through a great moment but a less good moment may arise tomorrow.

‘That’s why I try to simply enjoy the present without paying attention to the news.

Monza are believed to have slapped an asking price on Varela in the region of €40-50m (£33-42m).

Though they did not insert a buy-back clause in their deal with Monza for Varela, Benfica will be entitled to 20 per cent of any future transfer fee for the sought-after youngster.

The Primeira Liga club also have the right of first refusal should a bidding war break out for the Portugal Under-21 international, who was named the Serie A Rising Star of the Month for October.

Varela’s current contract with Monza runs through to June 2030.

Stamford Bridge was lit up last night by Fenerbahce fans' flares as Chelsea's home ground continued to host Shakhtar Donetsk's Champions League games.

The Ukrainian giants are this season playing their home European games in west London due to Russia's ongoing invasion of their home country, having in previous seasons staged their home games in Poland, Germany and Slovenia.

The matches have attracted local and travelling Ukrainian football fans, along with thousands of rivals supporters as Greek side AEK Athens and Portuguese outfit Sporting came to town earlier this season. Real Madrid will visit at the end of January.

Wednesday night saw Fenerbahce as the visiting team, and the fanbase came in numbers.

Stamford Bridge was glowing red from the light of flares ahead of the game, while footage of supporters descending on west London and the surrounding Chelsea area spread across social media.

As the designated away team, Fenerbahce were allocated the 'Shed End' of Stamford Bridge, which is remarked to hold around 6,000 fans, but thousands more were seen across 'home' sections of the stadium.

The tickets went on general sale earlier in November, which allows any member of the "general public" to purchase.

Fenerbahce won the game 1-0 and, speaking after the game, Ismail Yüksek remarked: “There were nearly 30,000 Fenerbahce fans in the stadium today.

"You wouldn’t see anything like this at any other club in the world. They gave us incredible support. They were amazing. They gave us incredible strength. I dedicate this victory to them.

"From the first minute to the last, the team fought just as hard as our fans. We deserved this victory from start to finish.".

Malaga's search for their first victory of the 2026-27 La Liga campaign will continue on Saturday afternoon when they welcome Athletic Bilbao to Estadio La Rosaleda.

Athletic have won two of the last three meetings between the two sides and also lead the overall head-to-head record 13 victories to Malaga's 11.

Malaga have a record of zero wins, five draws and eight defeats from their 13 league matches this season, with five points leaving them bottom of the La Liga table.

There is still plenty of football to be played this season, but they are right now seven points behind 17th-placed Valencia and will not want that to be stretched to 10 points in the next gameweek.

Juan Francisco Funes' side secured a return to La Liga through the 2025-26 Segunda Division playoffs, but they have found it tough to adjust to life back at this level.

Los Albicelestes will enter this match off the back of three straight losses to Real Betis, Racing de Santander and Osasuna, but they have managed to win once this season - a 3-0 success over Alcazar in the Copa del Rey at the end of October.

Malaga held Athletic to a 3-3 draw when the pair last locked horns at La Rosaleda, while their last win over the Basque side was a 2-1 success in October 2016.

As for Athletic, a record of four wins, four draws and four defeats from 12 matches has left them eighth in the table on 16 points, three points behind sixth-placed Sevilla heading into the next gameweek.

The Lions will enter this match off the back of a 1-0 defeat to Espanyol, which proved to be their first loss since October 21 away to Levante.

Edin Terzic's side have picked up 11 points from their seven home league matches this season, while they have claimed five points from their five games on their travels.

Athletic finished 12th in Spain's top flight last season, so there is clear room for improvement during the current campaign, with a European spot certainly the target.

The Lions will take on Numancia in the Copa del Rey in their first match of December before hosting Real Madrid in their next league game on December 6.

Adrian Nino has scored five times in nine appearances for Malaga this season, and the 22-year-old is set to continue in the final third of the field.

As for Athletic, Unai Eguiluz, Gorka Guruzeta, Maroan Sannadi and Dani Vivian will miss the match due to injury problems.

Head coach Terzic is expected to resist the temptation to shuffle his pack for this game despite the disappointment of the defeat to Espanyol.

Inaki Williams featured through the middle last time out, with Nico Williams to the left and Alex Berenguer to the right - that is again expected to be the case in this match.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

AC Milan have made a false start in their Europa League campaign, and they are running out of chances to put things right.

After losing three of their first four games in Europe, this morning’s edition of La Gazzetta dello Sport (seen below) writes that Milan must win away from home against Olympiacos to keep their hopes of reaching the round of 16 alive.

Read SempreMilan ad-free and get access to exclusive news. Click here for a free trial!

Recent findings suggest that in Athens, Ruben Amorim will put out his strongest side to try and do exactly that. Christian Pulisic and Diego Moreira will operate on the flanks, while Omari Hutchinson is set to feature behind Gonçalo Ramos. They have broken the mission down into four parts.

In Europe – a stage where Milan traditionally feel at home – the team has only truly looked comfortable against RB Salzburg, where they cruised past their opponents. Bournemouth proved to have too much, and even at San Siro Benfica and Ferencváros emerged with wins.

According to recent reports, one fact remains: while Milan are flying in the league, their attempt to take off in Europe never quite got off the ground. There is a gap that must be bridged: the distance between the Milan seen in European competition and the side so highly regarded in the league.

This extends to individual performances: the highly-praised Rabiot and Moreira have been instrumental in pushing Milan toward the Champions League spots domestically, yet they have yet to carry that form into Europe.

The Frenchman has tallied 5 goals and 6 assists in Serie A, but only one assist in European play. The Belgian has 4 goals and 4 assists in the league, yet has failed to produce a decisive moment in continental competition. It is time to bring that form onto the continent.

In the league, we see a Milan that never leaves its strongest players on the sidelines. In the wake of the defeat to Ferencváros – which followed a victory in the derby – Amorim remarked: “Perhaps we aren’t ready to be competitive every three days.” Now, the team must prove him wrong.

Hopes for European qualification depend on climbing from the current 28th-place position, which requires goals. Those goals are expected to come from Gonçalo Ramos. In the Rossoneri’s only European victory so far, he did get on the scoresheet, but it was the final one in a 4-0 rout.

So, it could hardly be described as a decisive goal. That is exactly the kind of contribution needed this evening at the Karaiskakis Stadium, where the Diavolo will fight for a chance to rejoin the pack within reach of the play-off spots at the very least.

Ramos is the man for the job: he is the current No.9, he has just returned to scoring in the league after a drought, and with January approaching, there is the prospect of a fresh influx of goals. Following the celebration against Frosinone, Amorim hopes for a repeat in Athens.

The narrative that he is a ‘team-oriented’ striker holds water and has served as a valid defence against those questioning his lack of goals given he ranks second in the league for successful hold-up plays, third for flick-ons, and boasts impressive statistics in ball recovery and defensive actions.

While these figures highlight his excellent team contribution, the financial investment of over €70m is also significant. From a forward who is a two-time European champion, it is only fair to expect goals that truly make the difference.

Sources indicate that another objective for this European night is to prove the team’s stature even without the immense Luke Modric, who is sidelined due to injury. Ardon Jashari will take his place, making Milan less focused on possession and more on aggression.

The style of play will mirror that of their opponents: individual duels – and, by extension, the intensity and approach to the match – will be more decisive than ever. While the squad has often been heavily rotated in previous European fixtures, this time it will feature the strongest XI available.

It has been revealed that jashari’s dynamism will need to come to the fore. Without Luka’s class and command of the tempo, the team’s playmaking dynamic shifts. Milan must turn this into an action-packed encounter, full of constant twists and turns, to avoid being sidelined by their opponents.

Sources indicate that assisting in this effort will be Rabiot and Pulisic, the latter acting as a vital link between the midfield and the attack. The required intensity should translate into a greater presence in the opposition’s hal. Ideally, right inside the penalty area.

According to recent reports, paradoxically, following the celebration against Frosinone, Amorim was the least satisfied: he had wanted more sustained pressure near or inside the opponent’s box. Now, necessity dictates this approach: a controlled game must give way to an all-out assault.

It has been revealed that beyond Jashari – who is expected to provide more running and pressing – Moreira remains another key weapon, thanks to his surging runs down the flanks. Meanwhile, Alphadjo Cisse and Hutchinson serve as options Amorim can call upon during the match should the team need a spark.

Climbing the standings is a must. Milan may sit fourth in the league, but they cannot afford to be twenty-eighth in the Europa League table. Moving up won’t be easy: the Greeks remain unbeaten (three wins and a draw) and have conceded only one goal.

Industry observers note that it is the joint-best defensive record in the UEL (along with Bayer Leverkusen). That is hardly an encouraging statistic for a Milan side that must score in order to win, because as things stand total elimination is on the cards.

According to recent reports, this would be a disgrace for a club aiming to reclaim its place as a major player on the international stage. There is still time to recover, however. Looking at the last two editions, 14 points (2024-25) and 16 points (2025-26) were enough to get into the top eight. Milan are on three, with 12 up for grabs.

So, Amorim’s side could even aim for direct qualification. However, a complete turnaround would be needed. So, the play-offs are more realistic, and – based on the figures from the last two editions – 9 or 10 points would be required in this case.

Milan would thus need to obtain another six or seven points from their upcoming matches against Sunderland (at home), Levski Sofia (away), and Ararat-Armenia (at San Siro). By no means an easy task, however.

Nicky Butt believes that Liverpool will prove to be Arsenal’s main title challengers over the likes of Manchester City this season.

Defending champions Arsenal extended their lead at the top of the table to six points after a hard-fought draw away at Newcastle.

Brighton had the chance to cut that lead to just three points, but a late Oli McBurnie brace saw them lose 2-0 to Hull City on Sunday.

Manchester City did snap their three-match losing streak, but a 1-1 draw on Fulham means Enzo Maresca’s side are now winless in four Premier League matches and also six points off the league leaders.

City will have the opportunity to eat into Arsenal’s lead at the top of the table when the two sides meet at the Emirates next week.

However, Butt does not expect them to last the course in this season’s title race, instead talking up Liverpool’s chances after their impressive 4-0 win over Manchester United on Sunday.

‘Any win for Liverpool against Man United or vice versa is massive,’ Butt said on The Good, The Bad & The Football podcast.

‘Forget the ten men or the level of the team they are playing against at the time. When Liverpool beat Man United or the other way around, it’s a massive result, especially for a new manager.

‘It was only a couple of years ago that they won the league, so they’re not a bad team, and they’ve added well.

Fears that Omar Marmoush has picked up an injury have been allayed after the Tottenham forward was pictured in training ahead of Sunday’s trip to Sunderland.

Concerns had grown online this week that Marmoush was set for a period on the sidelines, with speculation he was set to visit a knee specialist.

The 27-year-old came off the bench during Spurs’ 2-0 victory at home to Ipswich last weekend and did not appear to pick up an injury, as Roberto De Zerbi’s side returned to winning ways at the Tottenham Hotspur Stadium.

Inevitably, though, concerns had gained traction and Marmoush’s involvement against Sunderland had been considered doubtful.

Spurs have dismissed the claims as online speculation, and footage of Marmoush on the Hotspur Way training pitches was posted on the club’s social media on Thursday.

In a major boost for De Zerbi, who is at the moment sweating over the fitness of several attacking players, the Egyptian international now appears fit and available for selection.

Spurs are expected to be without wingers Mykhailo Mudryk, Mathys Tel and Savio against Sunderland, so Marmoush being able to deputise on the flanks as well as through the middle will give De Zerbi more options heading into the weekend.

Mudryk is still struggling with an ankle ligament injury, with De Zerbi suggesting last week the Chelsea loanee had suffered a setback in his recovery.

Tel, meanwhile, is expected to be out for up to three weeks after sustaining an ankle injury against Leeds before the international week.

With Mudryk and Tel absent against Ipswich, De Zerbi selected Savio in a matchday squad for the first time since October 10 after he suffered a muscular injury in training.

The Brazilian was introduced from the bench in the 64th minute, but had to come off again after suffering a recurrence of the muscular injury that had kept him out for the last six weeks.

Diogo Dalot may get the nod ahead of Noussair Mazraoui at right-back.

Pochettino has quickly settled on a midfield partnership of Kobbie Mainoo and Youri Tielemans, who was controversially sent off late on against Sporting but is available in the Premier League.

By Ben Sully | 26 Nov 2026 15:58, Last updated: 26 Nov 2026 16:04.

Inter Miami forward Luis Suarez has confirmed he is in talks with the MLS club over a fresh contract.

Suarez is in the closing stages of his third full season with Inter Miami after signing on a free transfer at the start of 2024.

The Uruguayan has scored 59 goals in 120 competitive appearances, including 17 strikes in 30 regular-season MLS games this season.

However, as it stands, Suarez is on course to become a free agent when his current deal expires at the end of the calendar year.

In theory, Friday's must-win playoff game against Columbus Crew could be his last, although he has revealed he is in talks over a fresh deal.

"We're already in talks with the club to find the best solution for both sides," Suarez told reporters on Wednesday.

"But honestly, my focus is more on the match against Columbus this Friday than on what will happen in the future.".

Inter Miami are one down in their three-match series against Columbus after falling to a heavy 3-0 defeat at the Nu Stadium on Saturday.

Gonzalo Tapia opened the scoring with a ninth-minute penalty, before Gonzalo Lujan's 36th-minute red card forced Inter Miami to play over 50 minutes with 10 men.

Columbus took full advantage to net two second-half goals to leave Inter Miami requiring a win at the ScottsMiracle-Gro Field to force a deciding game in the first-round tie.

Suarez has made it clear that "the time for excuses is over" as the Herons look to prolong their defence of the MLS Cup.

“It’s clear we are at a club where we have an obligation to win,” Suarez said.

Industry observers note that “If we get eliminated on Friday, it will be a disappointment. We have to be that clear about it.

"The time for excuses is over...it’s time to face reality. If we are eliminated, we will be the first to be self-critical, although we hope that doesn’t happen.

“I believe the squad are at a point where we understand that it’s time to deliver. This is our final opportunity.

"This format has given us another chance to play this Friday, and it’s the last shot we have to bring the series back home.”.

The visitors experienced disappointment in their last trip to Columbus in September, when they fell to a 2-1 defeat following a stoppage-time winner.

But Arteta admits Raya is still an injury doubt for Arsenal’s next Premier League fixture against City at the Emirates Stadium this weekend.

When asked after his side’s 2-2 draw with Dortmund, Arteta added: ‘We need to know first how bad it is and whether he has a chance or not in the next few weeks.’.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Rasmus Hojlund told Manchester City fans ‘there is only one club in Manchester’ after scoring for Napoli in their Champions League clash on Tuesday night.

Hojlund scored the opening goal in the second half at the Etihad Stadiumbut City salvaged a 2-2 draw following Rayan Cherki’s equaliser in the 86th minute.

After scoring his first Champions League goal of the season with a brilliant low finish past Gianluigi Donnarumma, Hojlund celebrating in front of City’s supporters.

But before turning to the half way line, the Denmark international held up one finger and told the crowd: ‘There is only one club in Manchester’.

When asked about his celebration after the game, Hojlund noted: ‘Some good banter, you know.

Recent findings suggest that ‘There’s the rivalry between Manchester City and Man United and obviously I have a past in Manchester United. That’s my club. Nothing against City but United is my home.’.

Former Red, Rasmus Hojlund scoring at the Etihad tonight:“There’s only one club in Manchester” 🔴⚪️⚫️😍 pic.twitter.com/mS5eQsMWRA.

Hojlund joined Manchester United in a £72 million deal from Atalanta in 2023 and spent two seasons at Old Trafford before his loan move to Napoli.

The 23-year-old then completed a £38 million permanent move to Napoli this summer as the Serie A club had an obligation to sign him after qualifying for the Champions League.

During his two seasons at United, Hojlund scored 26 goals in 95 appearances.

Cristian Gonzalez's side struggled after going a man down, accumulating just 0.99 expected goals (xG) to the Crew's 1.97.

The Herons' MLS Cup title defence could be over as soon as Friday if they lose at ScottsMiracle-Gro Field, while victory would see them force Game 3 back in Miami.

Suarez has urged his Miami team-mates "to deliver" in their win-or-go-home matchup against Columbus.

“I believe the squad are at a point where we understand that it’s time to deliver.

A week of hard work. One goal: Bring the series back to Miami. https://t.co/UBDPSHJHlf.

Miami boss Gonzalez shared the same views as his striker, and hopes his players will show their resilience in Game 2.

"It's not about feeling pressured, but rather acknowledging that we are at a club built to reach these stages.

"There are moments when you have to dig deep, tap into that sense of self-respect and the passion that drives you. That’s how I see the game, and I truly hope we can demonstrate that this Friday.".

Taha Habroune scored his first career playoff goal in Game 1, becoming the youngest player to score a playoff goal (20y 289d) for the Columbus Crew.

Habroune surpassed the previous record held by Edson Buddle (21y 127d) in September 2002, against the San Jose Earthquakes.

Lionel Messi recorded a goal and three assists in his last road playoff game in November 2025, against FC Cincinnati.

Messi is one of two players in MLS history to register four or more goal contributions in such games.

Despite a comfortable win for Columbus in Game 1, the Opta supercomputer expects a closer encounter, which could be decided by penalties, this time around.

With their 3-0 Game 1 win, Columbus have won consecutive games in the same season against Miami for the first time in club history.

The Crew have won both of their meetings with the Herons outside of the regular season (Game 1 and 2024 Leagues Cup Round of 16).

Industry observers note that saturday's victory was Columbus' 30th MLS Cup playoff victory. The Crew are the second team in MLS history with at least 30 playoff wins, joining the Los Angeles Galaxy (51).

Recent findings suggest that miami won a league-best 10 away matches during the regular season, but has just one win in five road playoff games (L4): a 4-0 win in the 2025 conference semi-finals at Cincinnati. When asked if that is case closed or if he will now be unavailable, Alonso said: ‘Closed.’.

Wesley Fofana has apologised after angering Chelsea fans with his interview on French YouTube channel.

Fofana smashed his penalty over the bar against Liverpool in October but saw the funny side.

It has been revealed that the YouTuber who conducted the ill-timed interview hit back at the coverage in England of Fofana’s quotes. Specifically, he was unhappy with how the focus was on Fofana joking about his penalty miss at Liverpool and what he mentioned about considering retiring from football. That was despite the YouTuber’s own social media channel posting those precise clips which led to widespread criticism.

Regardless, Fofana has now seen fit to apologise to Chelsea, but it remains to be seen whether Alonso will stick with the Frenchman and Levi Colwill for Friday’s trip to Nottingham Forest.

In a recent development, both Fofana and Colwill were bullied by Sunderland’s Brian Brobbey and Leeds United’s Dominic Calvert-Lewin, and Liam Delap is the next challenge. Alonso spoke of the ‘standards’ needed from his central defenders to deal with such strikers.

Delap will have a point to prove versus Chelsea, who sold him to Forest after a single season for £50million.

By Ben Knapton | 26 Nov 2026 16:00, Last updated: 26 Nov 2026 16:00.

England manager Thomas Tuchel has been told to consider an unusual solution to Harry Kane's injury absence if the Three Lions captain misses March's Nations League quarter-final with Norway.

Tuchel and co are sweating over the fitness of the Ballon d'Or winner after he was ruled out for a 'few months' with a serious ankle injury, sustained in Bayern Munich's 1-1 Bundesliga draw with FC Koln earlier this month.

Kane had to undergo surgery to correct the torn ligament, and there is a chance that he could now sit out the reunion with World Cup quarter-final foes Norway, whom the Three Lions face at the end of March 2027.

Tuchel has a plethora of alternative centre-forward options at his disposal, including Dominic Calvert-Lewin, Dominic Solanke, Ivan Toney, Ollie Watkins and Championship star Will Lankshear.

However, ex-England forward Brian Deane has exclusively told Sports Mole that Tuchel could instead consider using either Jude Bellingham or Morgan Rogers as a false nine rather than deploying a pure centre-forward.

“It is difficult because I do not think England have another centre-forward who can do exactly what Harry Kane does," Deane said. "He is not the quickest, but he is intelligent, drops into pockets and allows the team to rotate around him. He has earned the right for the manager to build that structure.

“Dominic Calvert-Lewin is very good at holding the ball up, bringing others into play and competing in the air. Whether he would score the same types of goals as Kane is another question.

In a recent development, “Solanke has the ability, but I am not convinced about his confidence at the moment. The England shirt can weigh heavily.

“Ivan Toney has a strong all-round game, is excellent in the box and is one of the best penalty-takers around. The question would be how he adjusts to the tempo of international football from the league he is playing in.

Sources indicate that “Will Lankshear is perhaps a little inexperienced. Bringing him into the squad is one thing; asking him to lead the line ahead of those other players is another.

Sources indicate that “Tuchel might decide not to use a conventional centre-forward. He could put Jude Bellingham or Morgan Rogers further forward and approach it differently. It is very difficult to replicate Kane. He has done amazingly well and is almost irreplaceable.”.

According to data from Transfermarkt, Bellingham has only made one club appearance as an out-and-out centre-forward, compared to 23 for Rogers during his career.

If Deane's prediction comes true and Tuchel does opt for a false-nine approach, the Chelsea man should therefore be at the head of the queue for striking duties, especially having also featured in that role for the Blues already this season against Tottenham Hotspur.

Bellingham has licence to continue in the number 10 role as a result, and Rogers being moved centrally opens the door for a fit-again Bukayo Saka to reclaim his place on the right flank.

However, there is every chance that Kane will recover in time to face Norway, aiming to build on an unparalleled record of 93 goals in 127 matches for his country.

Brian Deane was speaking to Sports Mole on behalf of BetWright.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Newcastle United look like a poor team playing badly. The evidence is increasingly damning after Matthias Jaissle’s side were loudly booed off at the end of this limp defeat.

This has all the makings of a long, hard season. Anger is already rising to the surface, even though Jaissle claimed Newcastle deserved more from a game they “controlled” in the first half and “dominated” in the second. Those comments jarred with what we had just seen.

After four years of enjoying an upward trajectory under Eddie Howe, the team faded last season, sold their best players in the summer, lost the manager and there is no evidence yet they have replaced anything with better.

Industry observers note that this was supposed to be a reaction to the embarrassing 4-1 thrashing at Coventry City, but it led to another loss and, in the first half at least, another abject display. Aston Villa were always the more fluent and more threatening. They should have won by more than just Johan Manzambi’s first-half header.

Johan Manzambi heads Aston Villa in front! 🟣 https://t.co/jxZf2568Sl.

According to recent reports, it is getting hard to comprehend what Jaissle wants his team to do. The much-hyped “vertical” style looks like an ugly incarnation of the long ball football of yesteryear. They did not like it at Newcastle in the 1980s and 1990s and some fashions should never return. It is in danger of resembling a shell suit that has emerged from the back of the wardrobe for a Saturday night out.

It has been revealed that there is so much confidence in the German in the Newcastle boardroom that they believe improvement is inevitable, but that is far from assured. Newcastle are not getting better; they are making all the same mistakes and, if anything, as an attacking force, they are looking increasingly stale and predictable. They did not have a shot on target in the first half and, other than one fantastic save in the second, Villa goalkeeper Zion Suzuki had nothing to do.

"If he doesn't slip Harvey Barnes in, he's got to hit the target" Shay Given discusses Newcastle's decision-making in the final third 🔲 https://t.co/wh4kCAEbxV.

It has been revealed that “Our decision-making in the final third was lacking today,” Jaissle mentioned. “I am frustrated, I understand the supporters’ reaction, that is their right [to boo after a defeat at home].”.

Industry observers note that it is time for a sharp dose of medicine on Tyneside. Expectations need to be adjusted, especially as none of the new signings have impressed. This was always the fear and the risk when you put all your faith in young players from abroad.

For Jaissle’s vertical football to work, Newcastle need to be able to win the ball high up the pitch, whether that is with a high press or competing for second balls from long passes. They do not do either well. More worryingly, they look so vulnerable, so easy to play through.

Villa did it to them all afternoon. Nicolas Jackson should have scored in the first half, Ibrahim Mbaye should have hit the target in the second.

On another day, Newcastle could also have had centre-back Sven Botman sent off for a lunge on Jackson. Then it really would have become ugly, but the Dutchman survived a VAR check.

Recent findings suggest that villa were always the better side. There was no fluency in Newcastle’s game, no structure, no patterns of play. Every time they turned over the ball, they looked stretched. Every time they got a set-piece, it was defended easily. Every time they went forward in the first half, the ball was sent aimlessly long and came straight back at them. In the second, they huffed and puffed but did not sustain any pressure on the Villa goal. The missed chances late on were not clear opportunities and they were snatched at by the hapless Yoane Wissa.

Newcastle were in disarray and it should have been 2-0 almost immediately when Emiliano Buendía received the ball in the middle of the area and crashed a shot against a post.

The home crowd tried to remain patient and supportive, but the sight of yet another long, aimless ball being punted forward straight to a Villa defender tipped some over the edge. There were boos and jeers in the stands while Jaissle screamed at Joe Willock and Wissa. There were more boos at half-time; things felt combustible.

Newcastle needed a big second half. They were better, but it was hardly anything to get excited about. A shot on the turn from Botman, superbly saved by Suzuki. Then a few half-chances were squandered, the occasional flash of a threat and that was it.

Newcastle will be relieved that this game is at St James’ Park, with the club having lost their previous two away fixtures 4-1 against both Coventry and Leeds.

Sources indicate that summer signing Nicolas Jackson has five goals in his previous six games for Aston Villa in all competitions and looks to be brimming with confidence as he leads the line for Unai Emery. The striker dispatched both finishes for his brace against Fenerbahce with unerring composure and will target more goals at St James’ Park.

One of the interesting subplots to this evening’s game will be watching Johan Manzambi playing for Aston Villa.

The Switzerland international’s decision to reject Newcastle in order to sign for Villa helped convince Eddie Howe to quit in the summer.

Having already missed out on Victor Munoz, who decided to join Liverpool at the last moment, losing Manzambi - their first-choice target across the position board - was a blow Howe did not feel he could recover from.

In short, he was not convinced the alternatives would give him the tools to do the job this season. Aladji Bamba, who was signed instead, has not started a game for Newcastle this season and appears to be well down the pecking order in the centre midfield under Howe’s successor Matthias Jaissle.

Manzambi had a slow start to his Villa career because of injury but he was hugely impressive at the World Cup for Switzerland and is expected to become one of the best midfield players in Europe over the next few years. Nobody can say with any degree of confidence that will be the same for Bamba.

Hello and welcome to our live coverage as Newcastle United welcome Aston Villa to St James’ Park in the Premier League.

Recent findings suggest that newcastle endured a hellish Monday night as they were condemned to an embarrassing 4-1 defeat by Coventry City in their previous top-flight outing. Matthias Jaissle’s rebranded Newcastle outfit have notably lacked consistency in the early weeks of the season, with the loss to Coventry another abrupt reminder of how this is expected to be a challenging campaign for his freshly assembled squad. The upcoming arrivals are yet to fully settle and Newcastle are undoubtedly still adapting following a turbulent summer transfer window where they lost several key players.

According to recent reports, meanwhile, Villa arrive up north in tremendously high spirits following their 6-0 thumping of Fenerbahce in midweek Champions League action, thereby recording their biggest European win in the club’s history. However, in a similar vein to Newcastle, Villa have struggled to impose themselves in the Premier League, triumphing just once in their opening six matches of the season. Unai Emery’s men conceded a 79th-minute equaliser to Brentford’s Kristoffer Ajer last time out in the Premier League to draw 2-2 and deepen their domestic frustration.

Despite how this week’s results have shaped contrasting moods in the two camps, Newcastle are presently three points ahead of Villa in the Premier League, with today’s visitors aiming to make it back-to-back top-flight away wins after beating Tottenham 3-2 in the capital last month.

Jaissle is still trying to find his feet in English football, and hosting Villa is yet another tough test of his credentials. Meanwhile, it’s a question of when Emery’s new-look Villa will click, not if, given his unbelievable impact at the club. The Spaniard is fast approaching his four-year anniversary as Villa’s head coach, and what a journey it has been.

We’ll bring you all the latest updates and drama from Tyneside. Kick-off is at 17:30, with team news coming shortly.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Unai Emery delivered a blunt assessment of Alejandro Garnacho’s situation at Aston Villa after the Argentine was left out of the squad for the defeat to Galatasaray on Tuesday night.

Villa were beaten 1-0 in Turkey and now sit ninth in the Champions League table, one place outside the automatic qualification spots.

Garnacho, meanwhile, trained with his Villa teammates on Monday but he was not even named on the bench against Galatasaray.

The on-loan Chelsea winger was also not included in Villa’s squad for their goalless draw at home to Sunderland on Saturday.

For the game against Galatasaray, Emery only picked 11 substitutes out of a possible 12 and also included two goalkeepers.

When asked about Garnacho’s absence after Villa’s defeat, Emery replied: ‘Today the players were here who I think are the best players to be here with us, to play with us.’.

Garnacho has made just seven appearances since joining Villa in the summer and is yet to score a goal or register an assist.

Villa have an obligation to buy Garnacho from Chelsea for £43 million but only if he makes a certain number of appearances this season.

Chelsea signed Garnacho in a £40m deal from Manchester United last year but the Argentine struggled to make an impact during his time at Stamford Bridge, scoring eight goals in 43 appearances.

Xabi Alonso still has injury challenges to solve as Chelsea look to put damaging defeats behind them on Friday night at Nottingham Forest.

Back-to-back losses to Sunderland and Leeds has put pressure on Alonso and his players as they head to struggling Forest.

In a welcome injury update, key midfielder Moises Caicedo has been declared fit to play less than a week after being forced off during the first half against Leeds.

But Alonso also confirmed that neither Joao Pedro nor Maxence Lacroix will be available.

Joao Pedro has been sidelined for a number of weeks with a thigh injury, during which time Chelsea’s form has taken a significant dip.

Young striker Emmanuel Emegha has deputised in the Brazilian’s absence, and he will hope his first goal for the club, coming last week against Leeds, will be enough to see him retain his place this weekend.

A decision must be made over whether to stick with the 4-2-3-1 system or revert to the 3-4-2-1 formation Chelsea were deploying earlier in the season.

It remains unclear when Joao Pedro, Jorrel Hato or Lacroix will return, amid suggestions that the latter could be back before the start of 2027.

Jamie Carragher believes Arsenal will beat Manchester City to end their Premier League title hopes on Sunday, while Thierry Henry claims Enzo Maresca’s side are ‘there to be dominated’.

Arsenal sit six points clear of City at the top of the Premier League and head into this weekend’s fixture off the back of a 1-1 draw with Borussia Dortmund in the Champions League on Tuesday night.

City, meanwhile, have registered just two wins in their last seven games in all competitions and needed to come from behind twice to draw 2-2 with Napoli in their Champions League game on Tuesday.

Enzo Maresca’s side visit the Emirates Stadium this weekend and Carragher feels Arsenal will be too strong for their Premier League title rivals.

In a recent development, ‘I think Arsenal will win. I can’t see City getting anything from that game,’ Carragher told CBS Sports after Arsenal’s draw with Dortmund.

‘They’ve been really poor of late, the results have shown that, not strong defensively at all.

‘Arsenal in the last couple of games have let in a couple of goals but I think they’ll be really tuned in to know if they beat Manchester City that’ll be end of Manchester City in terms of the title.

‘I think they’ll be really aggressive, man-to-man press, get after them all over the pitch. I just don’t see them [City] at all.’.

Asked who he believes can challenge Arsenal for the title, Carragher replied: ‘No one.

Use AI to go deeper into the stories you care about – powered by Metro and trusted publications.

Industry observers note that ‘And that’s not because Arsenal are amazing. Listen, they are a top team, don’t get me wrong, but in terms of the Champions League, I don’t think the Premier League teams can match… only Arsenal can really match what we’re seeing from the top teams.

‘And that shouldn’t be the case with the Premier League. The money we’ve got, the teams that we have, we have massive four or five teams who would all think they all have a real opportunity each season to win the league, spend big money, hundreds of millions on individual players, my own team being one in Liverpool. So to see how far we all are behind, besides Arsenal, they got to the Champions League final last season, you see City tonight, you see Villa lose, Liverpool lost a couple of weeks ago away to Fenerbahce.

Sources indicate that ‘I still think you’ve almost got four or five teams, Arsenal are one of them, the big teams in the Champions League. For the Premier League not to have more than one, considering we’ve got five in the competition and the funds they all have, it’s probably a bit disappointing and demonstrates why Arsenal are favourites for the Premier League.’.

Meanwhile, Thierry Henry believes City’s run of form shows that Maresca’s side could struggle to control the game against Arsenal at the Emirates Stadium.

‘You have two teams who have to rectify two things at the weekend – Arsenal, like we’ve been saying recently, and Mikel Arteta has been saying, when you’re on top of a team, don’t let them come back to attack like we’ve seen in the last two games,’ Henry said.

Recent findings suggest that ‘If you go back to City, and I’ve said it since the beginning of the season, the balance of the team isn’t right. Simple as that.

‘They have quality, they have goalscorers who will bail them out, Rayan Cherki bailed them out tonight, but the cohesion of the team, the way they don’t stop counters, they don’t control the game on and off the ball like they used to.

‘That didn’t stop them losing games under Pep [Guardiola] but they were more in control of games.

Industry observers note that ‘You have two teams who have been dominating the league in the last two, three years. But I want to see an Arsenal team that’s going to dominate City, and they are there to be dominated.

Sources indicate that ‘But on the other side, it might be the day that City wake up. But if they play the same way they’ve been playing recently, being open and all over the place in midfield, it could be a long day.’.

  • Mauricio Pochettino’s first match at Old Trafford as Manchester United head coach takes place on Saturday afternoon when Brentford visit the Theatre of Dreams for an intriguing Premier League contest.
  • While the Red Devils occupy a place in the relegation zone, sitting 19th in the Premier League table, the Bees are nine points and 13 places better off in sixth spot after 11 matches.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By Oliver Thomas | 26 Nov 2026 16:00, Last updated: 26 Nov 2026 17:04.

Mauricio Pochettino’s first match at Old Trafford as Manchester United head coach takes place on Saturday afternoon when Brentford visit the Theatre of Dreams for an intriguing Premier League contest.

While the Red Devils occupy a place in the relegation zone, sitting 19th in the Premier League table, the Bees are nine points and 13 places better off in sixth spot after 11 matches.

Chaos and drama seem to follow Man United wherever they go this season, as the Red Devils were involved in an action-packed 2-2 Champions League draw with Sporting Lisbon on Wednesday that saw them depart Portugal feeling aggrieved after a contest marred by contentious officiating.

Industry observers note that man United saw two goals chalked off in a match featuring three penalties and a late red card for Youri Tielemans. They were on course to claim victory via a quickfire Bruno Fernandes brace that overturned Luis Suarez's opening spot-kick, only for a Senne Lammens goalkeeping error to allow Suarez to salvage a share of the spoils for Sporting.

Pochettino was “so proud” of his players for how they handled “such a tough game” and believes that their performance was the “best medicine” to prepare for their next fixture in the Premier League, one they can ill-afford to drop points in if they wish to ease growing fears of relegation.

Two more goals conceded in Lisbon means Man United have shipped a total of 36 goals in 17 games across all competitions – more than any other side in Europe’s top-five leagues – while they have failed to keep a clean sheet in over 75 days (13 games) since a 4-0 UCL success over Sabah on September 10.

The Red Devils were put to the sword 4-0 by rivals Liverpool at Anfield in Pochettino’s first Premier League game in charge last weekend, leaving them second-bottom of the table with the fewest wins (one), second-most goals conceded (23) and on a nine-match winless streak in the top flight (D5 L4) – their longest such run since 1988-89.

Sitting just one point adrift of safety, Man United could climb out of the drop zone for the first time in three weeks with a victory over Brentford. The Red Devils have won only four of their last eight meetings with the Bees (D1 L3), but all four of those have come at Old Trafford, including a 2-1 success in April of last season.

Brentford travel to the red side of Manchester in buoyant mood after securing a comprehensive 4-0 home victory over Everton on Monday – their joint-biggest home win in the Premier League equalling their 4-0 thrashing of Man United in August 2022.

In a recent development, keane Lewis-Potter – who extended his contract with the club this week – scored two deflected goals before the Toffees were reduced to 10 men. Vitaly Janelt and Fabio Carvalho were also on target to help the Bees ease to their second win in three games and move to within four points of the top four.

Keith Andrews lauded his team’s “outstanding” performance against Everton and he now heads into Saturday’s fixture seeking to address Brentford’s contrasting home and away form, with only four of their 17 points accumulated on the road this season (D4 L1).

Including results from last season, Brentford are enduring their longest winless away run in the Premier League (10 matches – D7 L3) and their longest winless run on the road in any division since a 15-game streak in the Championship between April and December 2018.

The Bees will be aiming to end an eight-game losing run at Old Trafford and claim their first-ever Premier League away victory over Man United this weekend, as they bid to boost their early-season European ambitions and consolidate their place in the top six.

Manchester United Premier League form:.

Manchester United form (all competitions):.

Brentford form (all competitions):.

Man United are still having to cope without Carlos Baleba (hamstring), Benjamin Sesko (calf) and Manuel Ugarte (knee) due to injury, while Marcus Rashford (hip), Luke Shaw (fitness) and Karl Darlow (knee) are all doubtful.

A potential return for Shaw, who has not played since October 10, would likely see Lisandro Martinez either move back into the centre of defence or drop out of the side altogether, while Diogo Dalot is pushing to return at right-back at the expense of Noussair Mazraoui.

Leny Yoro’s red card against Liverpool has been overturned, allowing the youngster to start at centre-back alongside either Martinez, Harry Maguire of Matthijs De Ligt, who was handed a surprise first PL start in 357 days against Liverpool after a lengthy injury layoff.

Sources indicate that matheus Cunha is available to return from a European ban and will likely replace either Amad Diallo or Joshua Zirkzee. This would see former Brentford star Bryan Mbeumo either move back over to the right flank or start as a centre-forward.

As for Brentford, Igor Thiago is serving the second game of a three-match suspension, while Aaron Hickey (thigh), Nathan Collins (knee), Rico Henry (groin), Kaye Furo (ankle), Antoni Milambo and Josh Dasilva (both fitness) remain sidelined, the latter two are targeting a return before Christmas.

Mathias Jensen has scored more goals against Man United (four) than any other opponent in his career and the midfielder will be hoping to force his way back into the first XI at the expense of Mikkel Damsgaard.

Kevin Schade is another pushing for a recall in attack and could come in for either Dango Ouattara or Jaidon Anthony, while Callum Wilson could retain his starting spot as the central striker – he has never scored at Old Trafford in seven previous visits in all competitions.

Manchester United possible starting lineup:.

Lammens; Dalot, Yoro, Maguire, Martinez; Mainoo, Tielemans; Mbeumo, Fernandes, Cunha; Zirkzee.

Brentford possible starting lineup:.

Kelleher; Kayode, Van den Berg, Ajer, Lewis-Potter; Yarmoliuk, Janelt; Anthony, Jensen, Schade; Wilson.

Despite Man United’s dismal start in the top flight, Pochettino's first Premier League home match in charge should spark enough attacking urgency from the hosts to trouble a Bees side that has struggled on its travels.

Taking into account that each of the last six head-to-head battles has seen both teams score, while 12 of Man United’s last 14 home matches have produced over 2.5 goals, we can envisage a wide-open, end-to-end affair ending all square on this occasion.

Syndicated reporting provided by Stats Perform and reviewed by the SoccerNews editorial team.

Fabian Hurzeler expressed his delight with the performance of youngster Ibrahim Osman after Brighton cruised to victory over Universitatea Craiova in the Conference League.

The Seagulls won 4-0 at home on Thursday against 10-man Craiova, with Osman scoring twice while Maxim De Cuyper and Charalampos Kostoulas were also among the goals.

Osman provided an assist to go with his two goals, the first of which came inside three minutes, while he also led all players on the pitch for chances created (six).

Brighton dominated against their Romanian opponents, who saw Vladimir Screciu sent off in the first half for a high challenge on Matt O'Riley.

The Seagulls accumulated 2.63 expected goals (xG) from 27 shots, 10 of which were on target, while restricting Craiova to 0.11 from four attempts.

Hurzeler lauded the display of Osman, though he admitted his side could have been more clinical.

"I think he showed a really good performance today," Hurzeler said of 21-year-old Osman.

The Walcott has urged Arsenal star Noni Madueke to ‘big himself up more’ after Mikel Arteta revealed last night’s man of the match was frustrated in the wake of a 1-1 draw against Borussia Dortmund.

For the second match in succession, the Premier League champions threw away a lead and squandered numerous chances to record a convincing win.

Viktor Gyokeres opened the scoring with a blistering strike in the 10th minute, but the Sweden international, like many of his teammates, was profligate thereafter.

Ultimately, the Gunners were forced to settle for a point following Maximilian Beier’s second half equaliser and Mikel Arteta’s side are now likely to require two wins from their remaining three group stage games to secure a top eight finish and avoid a two-legged play-off in the Fresh Year.

In a recent development, madueke, meanwhile, walked away with the man of the match accolade after another lively display. The England international has been to the fore in recent weeks and, in the absence of Bukayo Saka, appears to have won the faith of the manager who raised eyebrows with his decision to sanctionthe decision to sign him from Chelsea in a £52million deal 18 months ago.

The 24-year-old was, however, far from pleased with a display that failed to help yield a win that Arsenal’s dominance deserved, according to Arteta.

‘Again he was really good, but if you were in the dressing room (you would see) he is not satisfied because he knows he had so many situations again that we can put the ball in the net or finish the action much better,’ remarked the Arsenal boss.

‘But again he was a real threat, he was super connected to the game with and without the ball. He was a real threat.’.

Walcott, meanwhile, agreed with his former Arsenal teammate and believes Madueke is showing signs that he is capable of maintaining a regular starting spot.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Jobe Bellingham revealed one of Borussia Dortmund’s coaches was responsible for identifying a ‘mismatch’ that helped his side earn a valuable Champions League point against Arsenal.

The Gunners could’ve been out of sight at half-time but had only Viktor Gyokeres’ spectacular early goal to show for their superiority.

Bundesliga table toppers Dortmund, were a different side immediately after the break and claimed a deserved equaliser through Maximilian Beier.

Dortmund’s physical approach and man-to-man system gradually saw them take control and they were millimeters from taking the lead when Bellingham was ruled offside and saw his close-range effort disallowed.

The 21-year-old was substituted shortly afterwards as was the Arsenal star he had be targeting having been instructed to make the most of a physical mismatch.

‘One of the coaches pointed out to me that I was against Myles [Lewis-Skelly],’ he explained on Amazon Prime Video.

Chelsea defender Wesley Fofana has apologised for an interview not authorised by the club that caused controversy this week.

The French centre-back was strongly criticised by fans following comments made about missing a crucial penalty during Chelsea’s Carabao Cup last-16 defeat by Liverpool last month.

Fofana spoke for two-and-a-half hours with YouTuber Zack Nani, who has since insisted on social media that “several quotes were taken out of context or plainly made up in England”.

It has been revealed that asked about the situation at a press conference held before Friday night’s trip to Nottingham Forest in the Premier League, Chelsea head coach Xabi Alonso stated: “We have addressed that with him [Fofana]. He has apologised.

“It was not right, he has said it is not going to be repeated, these types of things.”.

Fofana missed the decisive penalty that saw Chelsea’s Carabao Cup run end in the fourth round with a 6-5 shootout loss at Anfield following a 1-1 draw, blazing his spot-kick over the crossbar after Emmanuel Emegha had seen an effort saved by Giorgi Mamardashvili and Valentin Barco hit the woodwork.

He had also given away a penalty in normal time for handball that was converted by Cody Gakpo just three minutes after Morgan Rogers had given Chelsea the lead from 12 yards, continuing what has been a difficult season for him so far.

“The Liverpool match was tough to take, but I moved on rapidly because that’s just part of football,” Fofana was quoted as saying during the interview with Nani.

“I took responsibility for the penalty - I missed it - and, well, I knew I wasn’t a good penalty taker to begin with, you know [laughs]?”.

According to recent reports, he continued: “So, I just thought, ‘Okay, I’ll own it.’ But I ended up conceding a penalty during the match - it was a handball - but that’s just part of the game. I could have avoided it; it’s the kind of thing we talk about - you have to be consistent, and you have to keep improving in those areas.

“But after the penalty, I stepped up, because I’m one of the most experienced players. Out on the field, there were a lot of young guys. And, well, you had to get out there, you know?

Industry observers note that “You’ve got to go for it. And the way I look at it, if I fail, well, I’ve been through things. I’ve lived through a lot. If I fail, it’s not that it’s not a major deal - sure, it sucks, obviously - but as for me, if I’m the one being attacked, it’s no big deal.

Recent findings suggest that “In three days’ time, you win, and people forget. They’ve already forgotten about your penalty. That’s just how football works. I stepped up, took it, and missed.

According to recent reports, “I sent a real beauty of a shot way over the bar. Did you see my shot? I really blasted it high [laughs]. I remember a fan, way up high, he actually managed to catch the ball. But yeah, I missed, you know.

“Now, I laugh about it because it’s just part of football - that’s how it goes. And, well, there you have it.

“Besides, as I noted, we kept the momentum going, we got the win [against Manchester United three days later], and it sort of faded into the background. We actually saw a great response in the second half.”.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Former Chelsea and England star Shaun Wright-Phillips has urged Estevao to fight tooth and nail for a starting spot at Stamford Bridge and make himself ‘hard to ignore’ under Xabi Alonso.

Estevao burst onto the scene across an eye-catching opening campaign with Chelsea having joined the club from Palmeiras in the summer of 2025, racking up eight goals and four assists for the Blues.

A serious hamstring tear brought Estevao’s debut season to a premature end, though, a devastating blow that saw him miss out on a place in Brazil’s squad at this year’s World Cup.

Just days after Estevao sustained his injury, Chelsea decided to call time on Liam Rosenior’s turbulent managerial spell – and it has proven difficult for the 19-year-old to work himself back into the side since Alonso took charge.

The teenager had been limited to only two starts in the Carabao Cup approaching late October and rumours were beginning to circulate that he had grown frustrated with his peripheral role, with Barcelona reportedly keeping tabs on the situation.

However, Joao Pedro’s absence over the last month-and-a-half has created an opportunity for Estevao in Alonso’s attack and the youngster has started two of Chelsea’s last three games.

A humbling 4-1 defeat at the hands of Leeds may not have been what Estevao had in mind for his return, though, following a substitute appearance at Sunderland, and he will no doubt be desperate to banish those memories with a strong performance versus Nottingham Forest on Friday night.

Asked if he felt that Estevao still had a significant future at Chelsea under Alonso, Wright-Phillips told Metro, courtesy of kwiff: ‘It’s a hard one, because it seems like players at Chelsea outlive the managers, which is sad to say.

In a recent development, ‘That’s where modern football is going at the minute. It seems like players are outlasting coaches.

Use AI to go deeper into the stories you care about – powered by Metro and trusted publications.

‘But in general, that’s more of a tactical thing, in that Xabi plays more with wing-backs.

To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video.

Sources indicate that ‘If you play Estevao, you want him in the front three. Chances come in random ways, so he will get his chance again, and he has to do what he did the other day.

‘When he came on, I thought he was flying: not the weekend just gone, the weekend before that [against Sunderland. He came on and played really, really well.

‘So that’s him saying, “Look, I’m good enough to stay in your squad.” If he continuously does that, it becomes hard to ignore.’.

Another player whose development has hit something of a stumbling block in recent months is Malo Gusto, who, like Estevao, has found regular game-time hard to come by this season.

Reports just last week indicated Gusto could be open to the prospect of leaving Chelsea, with Manchester United understood to be among the right-back’s admirers.

Sources indicate that but when asked if it could be time to move Gusto on should a suitable offer come in for the Frenchman, Wright-Phillips replied: ‘Who do you replace him with? I think Gusto is a really fantastic player.

‘He might not be happy, which is understandable, because before Xabi came, when the other managers were there, his playing time was a lot greater, because it was either him or Reece James.

According to recent reports, ‘Reece James has had bad luck, he’s injured quite a lot, so Gusto got to play a lot. Whereas now, I think he’s better than a bit-part player, to be honest.

‘I haven’t watched him enough this season to turn around and say he should definitely be starting, but from what I saw of him last year and the type of player he is, I’d have him in my team at the drop of a hat, because I don’t think there are many right-backs out there that are gettable of that standard.’.

Chelsea splashed out in the region of £350million on new signings in the summer transfer window, including Morgan Rogers, who commanded a club-record fee of £117m when he joined from Aston Villa.

There were signs that the Blues were reaping the rewards of their significant spending in a promising start to the 2026/27 campaign, with Alonso’s all-star front three firing on all cylinders.

An injury to Joao Pedro has coincided with a concerning dip in results, though, and Alonso’s men were targeted with a chorus of boos as they exited the pitch following their latest setback on Saturday.

‘I think at the very beginning he demonstrated why he’s there, and at the minute it seems to have plateaued a bit. I don’t know what that’s from,’ Wright-Phillips stated when asked what he had made of Alonso’s start to managerial life in the Premier League, with Chelsea languishing down in eighth.

‘Playing as many games as they have, with the internationals that have come in the way they’ve come in, it feels like the Champions League is every week; it feels like it’s the Carabao Cup or something every week at the minute.

‘It’s going to take a bit of time for the players to get used to that change, where every game is a big game now for everybody; literally every game comes around very quick.

‘I think those clubs will settle down and get it together because they’re lucky to have the players within that squad to do that.’.

Pressed on whether there were any areas of the squad in need of strengthening in January, Wright-Phillips responded: ‘I’m not sure they need midfielders. I would say if they had two, or even one, solid defenders who can teach the other young ones there, that would be more than enough.

Industry observers note that ‘Chelsea have got an amazing squad. They’re missing that rock at the back; who will fight and die for everybody, because that rubs off on the team.

‘You might not like him, but that attitude and mentality will naturally rub off on you. Someone in the Thiago Silva mould.

‘They need to learn; they’re learning from each other. They’re good players, but to get to the top, most younger players and defenders learn off somebody with a lot more experience.’.

Switching his focus to the title race, Wright-Phillips, who represented Manchester City, Chelsea and QPR during his playing days, picked out Brighton as this year’s surprise package.

And while they were beaten in stoppage time by Hull City at the weekend, the ex-England winger is confident the Seagulls remain one of Arsenal’s ‘main challengers’.

‘No disrespect to Arsenal, but the best club for me in the Premier League this season, to watch and for output, is Brighton,’ Wright-Phillips – a Premier League winner with Chelsea in 2006 – explained.

‘Brighton are probably playing the best, but they’re not at the top of the league.

‘It can change and go a different way. I don’t think Arsenal are playing that well, and I don’t think City have played that well, but they’re the two teams that know how to get results when they aren’t playing to the level they know their maximum is.

‘Unfortunately for City, that hasn’t happened in the last four games, which is something they have to deal with and turn around.

‘The Christmas period is the right time to possibly do it, because all the games come quick and fast and the league table can change a dozen times in that time.

‘The main challengers to Arsenal would be Brighton and Manchester City as it stands. They’re the ones with the points on the board.

‘Until people start putting the points on the board, which is turning around, you’re seeing Liverpool sneak back up the table.

‘There will be other challenges as well, but leading into this Christmas period, I would say Arsenal’s challenger right now is Brighton and Manchester City.

Sources indicate that ‘Brighton, I think, are the only team to beat both of those two teams and do it nicely as well. It wasn’t a smash and grab.’.
